title: loom merge fails to detect commits ahead of main
description:
Two bugs in loom merge (push command):

1. **Fails to detect commits**: Running 'loom merge nova main' reports 'Already up to date (no new commits in nova)' even though nova has 14+ commits ahead of main (git log main..nova shows them). Had to fall back to 'git merge nova' which fast-forwarded correctly.

2. **Corrupts git config**: The 'detached HEAD approach' sets core.bare=true in the repo's local git config and doesn't clean it up. This causes subsequent git commands to fail with 'fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree'. Observed twice — once after 'loom merge nova main', and again after a successful 'git merge nova'. The workaround is 'git config --local core.bare false'.
close_reason: Fixed both bugs: (1) commit detection now uses correct git log ranges (target..source and remote/target..source), (2) push functions restore original branch via defer, detached functions now have self-contained cleanup

title: Add loom pr command to create PRs from worktree branches
description:
Add a new 'loom pr' command that creates a GitHub PR from a worktree branch to the main branch (or specified target branch). This is an alternative to 'loom push' which directly merges — instead, 'loom pr' creates a PR for code review before merging.

Usage:
  loom pr <worktree> [target]       # Create PR from worktree branch to target (default: main)
  loom pr --all                     # Create PRs for all worktrees with unpushed commits
  loom pr falcon                    # Create PR from falcon branch to main

Follow the same Cobra command pattern as push.go and pull.go. Register in Git Operations group. Support --all and --workspace flags. Use gh pr create under the hood. Auto-generate PR title/body from beads task. Push branch to remote first if needed. Skip worktrees with no commits ahead.

Key files: new internal/cli/pr.go, modify root.go and completions.go. Reuse Resolver, HasCommitsBetweenRemote, validateGitRef from existing code.

title: Kanban: Group by Epic swim lanes should auto-size height, not fixed
description:
When using any 'Group by' mode (Epic, Assignee, Priority, Type, Label), each swim lane has a fixed height regardless of content. This creates several problems across ALL group-by modes:

1. **Fixed height wastes space**: Lanes with only 1-2 cards still take up the same large height as lanes with many cards. Most space shows empty column placeholders ('No ready issues', 'No blocked issues', etc.).

2. **Cards scroll inside constrained lanes**: When a lane has many cards, they become scrollable within the fixed-height swim lane instead of the lane expanding to fit all cards.

3. **Page scroll required to see all groups**: With fixed-height lanes, you have to scroll the entire page to find groups further down. The catch-all groups ('Ungrouped', 'Unassigned', 'No Labels') tend to have the most items but are buried at the bottom.

4. **Empty columns take full width**: Columns with zero cards still show placeholder icons and text, wasting horizontal space.

Affected group-by modes tested:
- Epic: 3 epics + Ungrouped, most epics have 1-3 cards
- Assignee: falcon (2), nova (1), Unassigned (37) — massive imbalance
- Priority: P1/P2/P3/P4 — cards cut off at bottom of lanes
- Type: Bug/Epic/Feature/Task — Epic row shows 6 items but 0 in all columns (separate bug)
- Label: needs-revision (1), No Labels (39) — extreme imbalance

Desired behavior:
- Each swim lane should auto-size its height to fit its content
- No inner scrolling within swim lanes
- Consider collapsing empty columns or reducing their width
close_reason: Completed: CSS-only fix for swim lane auto-sizing. Changed flex properties and used CSS custom properties for contextual overflow behavior.

title: (BUG) claude.go SIGTERM race can signal wrong PID after process exits
description: In claude.go lines 83-91 (defaultClaudeNonInteractiveInvoker), there is a race condition in the shutdown goroutine. If the shutdown signal arrives between cmd.Wait() returning and close(done), the goroutine sends SIGTERM to a process that already exited. On Linux the PID could have been reused by another process, sending SIGTERM to an unrelated process. Fix: use a mutex or atomic flag to gate the signal send, or check process state before signaling. Add tests: test shutdown signal handling with a mock process that exits quickly, verify no signal sent after process exits.
close_reason: Already fixed. backend_claude.go uses atomic.Bool 'exited' flag (line 113). The goroutine checks exited.Load() before signaling (line 120), and cmd.Wait() sets exited.Store(true) before close(done) (line 137). Race condition is resolved.

title: Enhance /api/issues for Kanban: show all issue statuses with blocked info
description:
The Kanban board only shows ~5 open issues because it calls /api/ready which only returns open/in_progress from the daemon. 23+ review-status issues and blocked issues are invisible.

## Solution (designed and code-reviewed)

Enhance /api/issues with two new query params:
- exclude_status: comma-separated statuses to filter out server-side (e.g. closed,tombstone). Capped at 20 max to prevent DoS.
- include_blocked: when 'true', calls Blocked() RPC, merges blocked dependency info into each issue, returns KanbanIssue[] with is_blocked/blocked_by_count/blocked_by fields.

## Backend Changes (internal/webui/handlers.go)

1. Add KanbanIssue struct after IssueWithParent (line 32):
   - Embeds *types.IssueWithCounts + Parent/ParentTitle + IsBlocked bool + BlockedByCount int + BlockedBy []string

2. Add kanbanParams struct + parseKanbanParams(r) function (returns error, caps exclude_status at 20 values)

3. In handleListIssues:
   - Call parseKanbanParams(r) after parseListParams
   - After List RPC, filter out excluded statuses server-side (daemon ListArgs.Status only supports single value)
   - If include_blocked=true: call client.Blocked(), build blockedMap[issueID]*BlockedIssue, merge into KanbanIssue[] response
   - Handle json.Marshal errors (don't ignore with _)
   - Standard path unchanged (IssueWithParent[])

## Frontend Changes

1. types/issue.ts: Add optional is_blocked?: boolean, blocked_by_count?: number, blocked_by?: string[] to Issue interface

2. api/issues.ts: Add getKanbanIssues(options?: WorkFilter) that calls /api/issues?exclude_status=closed,tombstone&include_blocked=true

3. api/index.ts: Re-export getKanbanIssues

4. hooks/useIssues.ts: Add 'kanban' to mode union type, add branch calling getKanbanIssues(filter)

5. App.tsx: Use mode 'kanban' for kanban view. Derive blockedIssuesMap from enriched issue data (is_blocked field) instead of separate useBlockedIssues() fetch. Pass enabled: activeView !== 'kanban' to useBlockedIssues for backward compat.

## Verification
- curl 'http://localhost:8080/api/issues?exclude_status=closed,tombstone&include_blocked=true' returns all non-closed issues with blocked info
- Kanban shows 15 review issues in Needs Review column, 8 blocked issues in Blocked column
- go test ./internal/webui/... passes
- Frontend builds clean (npm run build)
close_reason: Completed: Enhanced /api/issues with exclude_status and include_blocked params for Kanban. Backend+frontend+tests all passing.

title: Fleet-DB Dual Backend Integration
description:
Integrate fleet-db as a dual issue-tracking backend alongside beads (Option C: Pragmatic Hybrid, 3-phase approach).

Users choose beads (local SQLite/git, via bd CLI) or fleetdb (Redis-backed, event-sourced, via in-process Go client) per project. Loomcli can auto-start an embedded fleet-db server using miniredis (dev) or connect to a real Redis (production).

## Phases
Phase 1: RunCommand adapter — working dual backend with zero caller changes (5 new files, 4 modified)
Phase 2: Typed hot-path methods — eliminate JSON round-trips on hot paths (~5 files modified)
Phase 3: Full migration — all data operations through IssueTracker, remove adapter (~7 files modified)

## Design Doc
docs/design/fleetdb-integration.md

## Key Decisions
- Dual backend: users choose beads OR fleetdb per project
- Config via loom.yaml, ~/.loom/config.yaml, and env vars (LOOM_FLEETDB_*)
- Configurable workspace mapping (fleet-db workspace key)
- Auto-start embedded fleet-db server (miniredis for dev, real Redis for prod)
- IssueBackend/IssueTracker interfaces with RunCommand for Phase 1 backward compat
- BDRunner stays for bd infrastructure commands (daemon start/stop, init, version)

title: Multi-Repo Workspace: Cross-repo project orchestration with shared beads
description:
Enable loomcli to orchestrate agents across multiple GitHub repos under a single workspace with a shared beads database.

## Concept
A Workspace is a cross-repo project:
- **Meta directory**: A parent directory containing a shared `.beads/` database
- **Single daemon**: One `loom serve` started at the meta directory
- **Repo affinity**: Tasks have explicit repo assignment, with future task-router support
- **Cross-repo agents**: Agents can work in different repos within the same epic

## Current State
- `LoomConfig.Workspaces` map and `WorkspaceConfig`/`RepoConfig` types exist in config.go
- `GetBeadsDir()` returns workspace path in workspace mode (correct for meta directory)
- `ResolveAgentTarget()` routes ALL workspace agents to workspace root (needs per-repo routing)
- `EnsureWorktreeBranch()` hardcodes `"origin/main"` (needs per-repo default branch)
- `AgentEntry` has `Worktree` but no `Repo` field (needs repo affinity)
- Web UI has no workspace awareness — single-repo assumptions throughout

## Phases
Phase 1: Backend — Per-repo agent routing and worktree management
Phase 2: Backend — Web UI API extensions for multi-repo
Phase 3: Frontend — Workspace view with repo tree sidebar
Phase 4: Frontend — Cross-repo agent orchestration UX

title: ResolveAgentTarget: per-repo worktree routing in workspace mode
description:
Fix `ResolveAgentTarget()` to route agents to their assigned repo's worktree directory instead of always using workspace root.

## Problem
At worktree.go:600, workspace mode always returns `wsConfig.Path` as WorkDir. This means all agents run `claude` from the workspace root, even when they should be working in a specific repo.

## Changes
- `ResolveAgentTarget()` should accept repo context (from AgentEntry.Repo)
- When repo is specified: create/find worktree under that repo's directory, return repo-specific WorkDir
- When repo is empty: keep current behavior (workspace root)
- `ResolvedTarget` may need a `Repo string` field for downstream consumers

## Key Constraint
The agent must still use the workspace-level `.beads/` for bd commands (shared beads). Only the git worktree and claude working directory should be repo-specific. This means `GetBeadsDir()` stays workspace-scoped (correct), but `cmd.Dir` for the agent process uses the repo worktree.

title: Add tests for monitor.go data collection functions
description:
## Summary

This task adds comprehensive unit tests for the monitor.go data collection functions. These functions gather agent status, task information, sync status, and statistics for the loom monitor dashboard. Testing them will improve code coverage and ensure reliability of the monitoring system.

## Technical Approach

Use the existing test infrastructure from testutil_test.go:
- **CommandMock**: Mock `execCommand` to stub bd/git command outputs with JSON responses
- **SetupTestWorktree**: Create mock worktree directory structures
- **SetupTestEnv**: Configure environment variables (LOOM_WORKTREES_DIR)

The tests will:
1. Mock external command outputs (bd, git) to simulate various scenarios
2. Create temporary directories with lock files to test lock detection
3. Verify correct parsing of JSON responses from bd commands
4. Test error handling when commands fail

## Files to Modify

### internal/cli/monitor_test.go
Add new test functions for the data collection functions:

1. **TestRunBdCommand** - Tests the bd command wrapper
   - Success case with stdout
   - Error case when command fails

2. **TestCollectStatistics** - Tests statistics collection
   - Normal case with valid JSON from `bd stats --json`
   - Empty stats (no issues)
   - Command failure returns zero values

3. **TestCollectSyncStatus** - Tests sync status collection
   - Synced state (no errors in output)
   - Unsynced state (error in output)
   - Count git push/pull needs from agents

4. **TestCollectTaskStatus** - Tests task categorization
   - Tasks with design go to ReadyToImplement
   - Tasks without design go to NeedsPlanning
   - Tasks with [Need Review] in title go to NeedReview
   - In-progress tasks populate InProgressTasks and agentTasks map
   - Blocked tasks from `bd blocked`
   - Epics are skipped
   - Top 5 limit for each category
   - JSON parsing errors handled gracefully

5. **TestCollectAgentStatus** - Tests agent/worktree status determination
   - Agent with running lock shows lock status (planning/working)
   - Agent with task ID in lock shows task
   - Agent with closed task shows "done:"
   - Agent with no lock and clean worktree shows "ready"
   - Agent with no lock and dirty worktree shows "X changes"
   - Agent with in_progress task but no lock shows "error:"
   - Task ID fallback from agentTasks when lock has "..."
   - Task conflict detection (multiple agents same task)
   - Ahead/behind counts from git

6. **TestCollectMonitorData** - Integration test for complete data collection
   - Verifies all sections populated
   - TaskConflicts map populated correctly

## Dependencies

- Existing test utilities in testutil_test.go (CommandMock, SetupTestWorktree, SetupTestEnv)
- Standard library testing package
- encoding/json for test data

## Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **JSON parsing failures**: When bd returns invalid JSON, functions should return zero/empty values
2. **Command execution failures**: When bd/git commands fail, functions should gracefully handle
3. **Empty worktrees**: When no worktrees found, return empty agent list
4. **Missing lock files**: Correctly determine agent status without locks
5. **Stale locks**: Process not running but lock exists (handled by CheckLock)
6. **Unicode in output**: displayWidth already tested, but verify in integration

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
Each function tested in isolation with mocked dependencies. Example:

```go
func TestCollectStatistics(t *testing.T) {
    mock := NewCommandMock(t, []CommandStub{
        {Name: "bd", Args: []string{"stats", "--json"},
         Stdout: `{"summary":{"total_issues":10,"open_issues":3,"closed_issues":7}}`},
    })
    mock.Install()

    stats := collectStatistics()

    if stats.Total != 10 { t.Errorf("expected Total=10") }
    if stats.Open != 3 { t.Errorf("expected Open=3") }
    if stats.Closed != 7 { t.Errorf("expected Closed=7") }
    if stats.Completion != 70.0 { t.Errorf("expected Completion=70%%") }
}
```

### Integration-style Tests
Test collectAgentStatus with real lock files in temp directories:

```go
func TestCollectAgentStatus_WithLock(t *testing.T) {
    // Setup temp worktrees directory with lock file
    // Mock git commands for branch/status
    // Verify lock status reflected in agent status
}
```

### Manual Verification
1. Run `go test -v ./internal/cli -run TestCollect` to see all new tests pass
2. Run `go test -cover ./internal/cli` to verify coverage improvement
3. Inspect test output for correct assertions

title: Drift branch code review: 33 issues from 8-agent review
description: Epic tracking all findings from the 8-agent parallel code review of the drift branch (~170 commits). Issues organized by severity: 14 critical, 19 important. All fixes must follow test-first approach: write a failing test that reproduces the bug, then fix the code to make it pass.

title: [CRITICAL] Move-issue uses same-workspace connection pool for target
description:
handlers_move.go:243 — The handler fetches one connection from the pool and uses it for ALL operations including creating the issue in the 'target' workspace. But pool.Get() always returns the current workspace's daemon. The move operation silently clones the issue in the same workspace and closes the original. Needs MultiPool dispatch by workspace name.

Test coverage: Test exists (handlers_move_test.go) but MASKS the bug — single mock pool structurally mirrors the production bug; never tests cross-workspace Create.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write a test with a multi-pool mock that returns different clients per workspace name. Verify Create is called on the target workspace's client, not the source's. Then fix the handler to use MultiPool.
notes: COMPLETED by falcon. Code fix was already in place from prior work (pulse). Added 2 missing ownership verification tests: TestMoveIssue_CrossWorkspace_ClientsReturnedToCorrectPools and TestMoveIssue_CrossWorkspace_TargetGetError_SourceReturned. make gate passes. Push blocked by flaky internal/cli git tests (TestCaptureGitDiff*, TestResolveMergeBase*) caused by dirty worktree state from parallel agents — not related to this change. Commit: 89bdc567 on falcon branch.

title: [CRITICAL] resolveAgentRepos returns empty slice — disables filtering
description:
daemon_repos.go:9-52 — When all repo groups are unknown, returns []string{} (non-nil, length 0). LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS is never set, so the agent claims tasks from any repo — opposite of intent.

Test coverage: daemon_repos_test.go exists but no test for 'all groups unknown → empty result' case.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: resolveAgentRepos with agent declaring RepoGroups=["nonexistent"], assert error is returned (not empty slice). Then fix: return error when Repos/RepoGroups are declared but resolve to nothing.

title: [CRITICAL] Tab reset on issue change omits SESSIONS_TAB
description:
IssueDetailPanel.tsx:481 — useEffect on issue?.id resets tabs to [DETAILS_TAB] only. If no persisted state exists, Sessions tab is permanently missing after navigating between issues.

Test coverage: No tests exist.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: render IssueDetailPanel, change issue ID, assert tabs include SESSIONS_TAB when no persisted state. Then fix: reset to [DETAILS_TAB, SESSIONS_TAB] consistently.

title: [CRITICAL] Optimistic status updates use stale closure
description:
useOptimisticStatusUpdate.ts:137-166 — applyOptimisticUpdate uses direct map write from closure-captured issues, not functional setIssues. Concurrent updates to different issues clobber each other.

Test coverage: Test exists (useOptimisticStatusUpdate.test.ts:592) but MASKS the bug — Promise.all inside act() resolves both before checking; doesn't detect inter-render clobber.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test that fires two updates in separate act() calls without awaiting the first, then asserts both optimistic changes are visible simultaneously. Then fix: change to functional setIssues((current) => ...) form.

title: [CRITICAL] Fallback polling never activates under flapping SSE
description:
useFallbackPolling.ts:141-171 — Each connected→reconnecting transition restarts the activation countdown. A repeatedly-failing connection never triggers fallback polling because each brief reconnect clears the timer.

Test coverage: useFallbackPolling.test.ts exists but only tests initial mount in reconnecting state, not connected→reconnecting oscillation.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: simulate wsState cycling connected→reconnecting→connected→reconnecting within 30s, assert polling eventually activates despite oscillation. Then fix: track first degraded-episode timestamp, only reset on sustained connected state.

title: [CRITICAL] Escape registry module-level leak across component trees
description:
useKeyboardShortcuts.tsx:112-151 — Module-level mutable singletons (layers[], layerIdCounter, escapeListenerAttached) persist across React trees and test suites. Cross-contamination between KeyboardShortcutProvider instances; no afterEach cleanup in tests.

Test coverage: useKeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx exists but has no afterEach module state reset and no cross-provider test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: mount two KeyboardShortcutProviders, register escape layers in each, assert they don't interfere. Add afterEach that resets module state. Then fix: use React context-scoped registry (useRef at provider level) instead of module-level.

title: handleTitleSave silently swallows errors
description:
IssueDetailPanel.tsx:645-658 — No catch block. API failure sets spinner back to false but no error toast shown, no revert of optimistic title. Inconsistent with handleStatusChange/handlePrioritySave which all catch and surface errors.

Test coverage: EditableTitle.test.tsx tests the component, not the IssueDetailPanel callback wiring.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: mock updateIssue to reject, call handleTitleSave, assert error state is set and toast is shown. Then fix: add catch block matching the pattern used in handleStatusChange.

title: SSE broadcast hardcodes DefaultWorkspace for terminal sessions
description:
handlers_terminal.go:357 — tabMetaStore.Get() hardcodes workspace to 'default' regardless of actual workspace. For non-default workspaces, Get returns nothing, SSE event is never broadcast, issue session activity indicator stays stale.

Test coverage: handlers_terminal_test.go tests with DefaultWorkspace only; no non-default workspace scenario.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: create session in 'myproject' workspace, establish WebSocket, assert SSE event is broadcast with correct workspace. Then fix: pass workspace as query param in WebSocket URL and validate in handler.

title: handleCloseOthers deletes pinned tabs
description:
useTabOrdering.ts:45-56 — handleCloseOthers(tabId) filters to all others including pinned tabs and calls deleteTab on each. Pinned tabs are supposed to be protected from mass-close.

Test coverage: No tests exist.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: create 3 tabs (one pinned), call handleCloseOthers on an unpinned tab, assert pinned tab survives. Then fix: filter to tabs.filter(t => t.id !== tabId && !t.pinned).

title: Escape sequence skip hardcoded to 2 — breaks multi-byte CSI
description:
slashCommandInterceptor.ts:82-87 — escapeSeqRemaining set to 2, correct for ESC[A (3 bytes) but wrong for ESC[1;5A (Ctrl+Up, 7 bytes). Parameter bytes are treated as printable chars and appended to command buffer, corrupting slash commands.

Test coverage: slashCommandInterceptor.test.ts:326 only tests 3-byte ESC[A; no test for extended sequences.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: enter /hel, send ESC[1;5A (Ctrl+Up), continue typing 'p', assert buffer is '/help' not '/hel1;5p'. Then fix: either exit command mode on ESC, or implement full CSI parser that reads until terminating alpha byte.

title: Panel close skips terminal session cleanup
description:
IssueDetailPanel.tsx:403-420 — closeTab calls deleteTabMetadata and scheduleSessionKill for explicit close. But closing the panel or navigating to a different issue resets tabs to [DETAILS_TAB] without calling closeTab for terminal tabs. Tmux sessions remain running on server.

Test coverage: No tests exist.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: open panel with terminal tab, change issue ID, assert deleteTabMetadata and scheduleSessionKill were called for the terminal tab. Then fix: add cleanup effect that runs on issue change / panel close, calling cleanup for all terminal tabs (capture tabs in a ref to avoid stale closure).

title: [CRITICAL] fleetDB.Ready silently drops Labels and SourceRepos

fleetdb_backend_tracker.go:20 — opts.Labels and opts.SourceRepos are never forwarded to rpc.ReadyArgs. Multi-repo label filtering is completely non-functional with fleet-db backend. Agents receive tasks from all repos instead of their assigned one. 100% confidence.

Test coverage: Tests exist (fleetdb_parity_test.go, fleetdb_backend_test.go) but DON'T cover Labels/SourceRepos — ReadyOpts{Limit: 50} only.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Add test in fleetdb_backend_test.go that passes ReadyOpts{Labels: []string{"repo:backend"}, SourceRepos: []string{"repo-a"}} and asserts args.Labels and args.SourceRepos are forwarded. Test will fail. Then add Labels: opts.Labels, SourceRepos: opts.SourceRepos to the rpc.ReadyArgs literal.
notes: Fix committed as d40623ec. Push blocked by pre-existing test failures in pre-push hook (workspace/worktree/git-diff tests fail due to branch name conflicts in worktree environment). The fix itself is verified correct — all fleetdb tests pass with race detector. These pre-push failures reproduce on any push from this worktree.

title: Transcript tool_input rendered with no length cap

SessionDetailView.tsx:149 — entry.tool_input (raw JSON from agent session, can be full file contents) rendered as-is with no truncation. Large tool inputs flood the DOM and degrade UI performance.

title: ResizeDivider stale isDraggingRef on remount
description:
ResizeDivider.tsx:28 — isDraggingRef is not reset on unmount cleanup. If component remounts quickly during drag (rapid tab switching), stale lastYRef produces incorrect initial delta causing jarring jumps.

Test coverage: ResizeDivider.test.tsx exists but no unmount/remount drag-in-progress test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: start drag, unmount, remount, first move event, assert delta is calculated from fresh position not stale lastYRef. Then fix: reset isDraggingRef.current = false in unmount cleanup.

title: DiffTab global error shown for per-file failures
description:
DiffTab.tsx:101-103 — error is the global hook error, not per-file. When one file fetch fails, error.message is shown for ALL expanded non-cached files. Also, file-list error and patch error are semantically conflated.

Test coverage: DiffTab.test.tsx tests error rendering but not multi-file error misattribution.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: expand two files, fail fetch for file A, assert file B shows loading (not file A's error). Then fix: track per-file error state in useDiff (e.g., patchErrors Map or discriminated union cache entries).

title: parsePatch breaks on embedded @@ in file content
description:
DiffFileViewer.tsx:33-70 — Any line starting with @@ in diff content is treated as a new hunk header. If regex match fails, a new Hunk object is still created with oldNum/newNum=0, corrupting line numbers for all subsequent lines.

Test coverage: DiffComponents.test.tsx tests parsePatch but all tests use well-formed diffs; no embedded @@ in content.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: parsePatch with a diff containing '@@' in file content (e.g., assembly listing), assert line numbers are correct throughout. Then fix: only create new hunk if regex matches.

title: validateDiffPath uses path.Clean not filepath.Clean
description:
handlers_diff.go:44-57 — Uses 'path' package (POSIX-only) instead of 'path/filepath' (OS-aware). Inconsistent with handlers_files.go which uses filepath.Clean. Not exploitable but maintainability issue.

Test coverage: git_test.go validates ref strings, not path cleaning behavior. Tangential coverage.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test with OS-specific path separator if applicable. Then fix: change import from 'path' to 'path/filepath', use filepath.Clean. Simple one-liner.

title: validateGitRef weaker than HTTP-layer regex
description:
git.go:13-18 — CLI-level validateGitRef only rejects refs starting with '-'. HTTP-layer validGitRef regex requires [a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_./-]*. Defense-in-depth gap: any future non-HTTP caller of DiffFilePatch/DiffFiles would only be protected by the weak validator.

Test coverage: git_test.go tests the CLI validator which is the weak one.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: validateGitRef('--upload-pack=evil') should fail. validateGitRef('HEAD~1; rm -rf /') should fail. Then fix: align CLI validator with HTTP regex, or at minimum reject '--' and '..'.

title: Workspace cache null window during mutations
description:
workspace.ts:183-197 — setDefaultWorkspace/createWorkspace increment cacheGeneration and null workspaceCache before refresh completes. Components calling getCachedWorkspace() synchronously in this window get null. Concurrent mutations cause generation races.

Test coverage: workspace.reorder.test.ts and App.test.tsx test happy path; no concurrent mutation test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: call setDefaultWorkspace twice concurrently, assert getCachedWorkspace() never returns null during the window. Then fix: hold prior cache value until refresh completes before clearing.

title: No debounce on drag/keyboard reorder — last-write-wins race
description:
WorkspaceTree.tsx:244-260 — Each handleDragEnd fires PUT /api/workspace/order without waiting for prior request. Rapid reorders produce non-deterministic server state. Rollback only on error, not on out-of-order responses.

Test coverage: workspace.reorder.test.ts exists but no rapid-consecutive-reorder test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: fire two reorders in quick succession, assert only the last order is sent to server (debounced). Then fix: add ~300ms debounce on the reorder API call.

title: stateRef non-null assertion crash on race
description:
useWorkspaceState.ts:101 — captureSnapshot uses stateRef.current! non-null assertion. If switchWorkspace is called before parent mounts and sets stateRef (e.g., deep-link popstate event), crashes with Cannot read properties of null.

Test coverage: useWorkspaceState.test.ts tests with populated ref; no pre-mount call test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: call captureSnapshot before stateRef is populated, assert it returns default snapshot (not crash). Then fix: add if (!stateRef.current) return defaultSnapshot guard.

title: useTabInit stale sessionStorage races with server restore
description:
useTabInit.ts:66-71 + TerminalView.tsx:229-236 — Two mechanisms restore active tab on page load: useTabInit reads sessionStorage synchronously, useSessionRestore fetches from server async. Server response overwrites user selection in the brief window. sessionStorage read in useTabInit is effectively dead code.

Test coverage: useTabInit.test.ts exists but unclear if race scenario is tested.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: set sessionStorage active tab, mock server returning different tab, assert no tab flicker during load. Then fix: remove sessionStorage read from useTabInit, rely on useSessionRestore with sessionStorage as offline fallback.

title: [CRITICAL] fleetDB.List silently drops ParentID
description:
fleetdb_backend_tracker.go:36 — opts.ParentID is never populated into rpcArgs. Epic PR creation (daemon_pr.go:94) lists ALL issues instead of only the epic's children. 100% confidence.

Test coverage: Test exists (fleetdb_backend_test.go:232) but asserts Status/Assignee/Type/Limit — never checks ParentID.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Add assertion in TestFleetDBBackend_List: pass ListOpts{ParentID: "epic-1"} and assert args.ParentID == "epic-1". Test will fail. Then add ParentID: opts.ParentID to the rpc.ListArgs literal.

title: CSP report handler logs untruncated fields
description:
handlers_csp.go:145-152 — document_uri, violated_directive, blocked_uri, source_file logged directly from untrusted input without per-field length truncation. Body is capped at 10KB but a single field can be nearly 10KB. Inconsistent with handlers_client_errors.go which truncates every field.

Test coverage: handlers_csp_test.go exists but no test for oversized field values.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: submit CSP report with 10KB document_uri, assert logged value is truncated to 2048 bytes. Then fix: add truncation constants (2048 for URIs, 512 for directives) matching handlers_client_errors.go pattern.

title: Proxy debug logging leaks auth tokens in query string
description:
loom_proxy.go:131-132, 144-145 — ErrorHandler and Director use r.URL.String() which includes full query string. WebSocket/SSE auth tokens in ?token= are written to logs when LOOM_PROXY_DEBUG=1. Core middleware correctly uses r.URL.Path only.

Test coverage: No tests exist.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: set LOOM_PROXY_DEBUG=1, send request with ?token=secret, capture log output, assert 'secret' is not present. Then fix: replace r.URL.String() with r.URL.Path in both log statements.

title: mockFleetDBClient nil response causes panic in tests
description:
fleetdb_backend_test.go:40-73 — Show, Stats, Update, CloseIssue return nil, nil when fn not set. Production code dereferences resp without nil check (resp.Success panics). Any future test exercising these methods without setting mock fn will panic not fail.

Test coverage: N/A — this IS the test infrastructure.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: call b.GetIssue without setting showFn, assert test failure not panic. Then fix: change defaults to return &rpc.Response{Success: true, Data: json.RawMessage("null")}, nil matching Ready/List/Blocked pattern.

title: GetIssueText returns JSON from fleet-db vs human text from bd
description:
fleetdb_backend_tracker.go:98-107 — fleetDBBackend.GetIssueText returns raw JSON (resp.Data), while bdBackend returns human-readable text from 'bd show'. Used in recover.go to prompt Claude for completion classification — JSON degrades signal quality vs concise description. No parity test exists.

Test coverage: fleetdb_backend_test.go and recover_test.go exist but mock returns human text format; no parity test for this method.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write parity test: call GetIssueText on both backends with same issue, assert both return human-readable format (not JSON). Then fix: have fleetDBBackend format IssueDetails as 'Title: X\nStatus: Y\nDescription: Z' rather than returning raw JSON.

title: SSE filter passes mutations with empty source_repo to all clients
description:
sse.go:103-108 — matchesSourceRepoFilter returns true when sourceRepo is empty, regardless of client filter. MutationRefresh events from pollDBChanges never set SourceRepo, so they bypass all filters. A client scoped to repo-a still sees refresh events from repo-b changes.

Test coverage: sse_test.go exists but no test for empty source_repo with filtered client.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: register client with source_repos=[repo-a], broadcast mutation with empty source_repo, assert client receives it (document intentional fan-out) OR assert client doesn't receive it (fix filtering). Then decide on semantics and implement.

title: diffAgents uses reflect.DeepEqual — fragile to unexported/derived fields
description:
daemon_reconciler.go:216 — reflect.DeepEqual on AgentEntry compares ALL fields including SourceRepos (yaml:"-" json:"-"). Currently safe because SourceRepos is always nil on both sides. But if daemon ever caches resolved SourceRepos on the in-memory entry, diffAgents would detect phantom 'modified' entries triggering unnecessary drain/restart.

Test coverage: daemon_reconciler_test.go exists but no test for this edge case.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: two AgentEntry structs identical except SourceRepos field, assert diffAgents returns no modifications. Then fix: use explicit field comparison or a dedicated Equal method instead of reflect.DeepEqual.

title: isMultiRepo JSDoc says 2+ but code uses 1+
description:
useWorkspaceContext.tsx:100,330 — JSDoc on WorkspaceContextValue says 'True when workspace has 2+ repos' but implementation uses >= 1. Stale doc creates contract mismatch for future maintainers.

Test coverage: useWorkspaceContext.test.tsx:738 confirms 1+ is intentional. But JSDoc is wrong.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Existing test already validates the behavior. Fix: update JSDoc at line 100 to 'True when workspace has 1+ repos'. One-line change.

title: useFocusTrap document-level listener conflicts with concurrent traps
description:
useFocusTrap.ts:56-90 — Tab handler added to document, not containerRef. Two simultaneously active traps (e.g., modal over panel during transition) both intercept Tab. No mutual exclusivity mechanism unlike the escape layer registry.

Test coverage: useFocusTrap.test.ts exists but no test for two concurrent active traps.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: mount two components with useFocusTrap(_, true), press Tab, assert only the top-layer trap handles it. Then fix: add trap priority mechanism or document single-active-trap constraint.

title: migrateLocalStorage QuotaExceeded handler re-reads key instead of reusing
description:
migrateLocalStorage.ts:55-66 — Inner QuotaExceededError handler re-fetches localStorage.getItem(v5Key) instead of reusing the already-captured outer oldValue (which is out of scope). If v5Key was already removed by concurrent code, migration silently drops data.

Test coverage: migrateLocalStorage.test.ts tests QuotaExceeded but doesn't test the re-read-returns-null scenario.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: mock getItem to return null on second call (simulating concurrent removal), assert migration doesn't silently lose data. Then fix: declare let oldValue before the try block so catch can access it.

title: ConnectionBanner stale indicator never auto-updates without parent re-render
description:
ConnectionBanner.tsx:61-62 — isStale and formatRelativeTime use new Date() at render time. If parent doesn't re-render after SSE disconnect, these values freeze. Banner shows 'just now' for up to 5 minutes. Stale styling never appears until external re-render.

Test coverage: ConnectionBanner.test.tsx:192 tests stale indicator but uses fixed Date mocks, not passage of time.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: render with lastUpdated=now, advance fake timers by 6 minutes without re-rendering parent, assert data-stale='true' is set. Then fix: add setInterval-based local state tick at 1s resolution while banner is visible.

title: [CRITICAL] prUrl lacks scheme validation — potential XSS
description:
IssueDetailPanel.tsx:942, IssueHeader.tsx:139 — isPRUrl only checks for /pull/ substring. A javascript: URL containing /pull/ passes the check and lands in <a href>. React's protection is not universal.

Test coverage: issueCategory.test.ts tests category classification, not href safety. No scheme validation test exists.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test that isPRUrl('javascript:alert(1)//github.com/x/y/pull/1') should return false or that the rendered <a> enforces https scheme. Then add scheme validation: require https:// or http:// prefix before propagating prUrl.

title: Supervisor retries permanently on static repo misconfiguration
[CRITICAL] Stale diff cache — no invalidation on new commits
description:
useDiff.ts:100-121 — Patch cache is permanent until agent changes. No TTL, no invalidation on commit. fetchInProgressRef is never reset when enabled transitions false->true, so reopening the diff tab shows stale data for an actively running agent.

Test coverage: DiffTab.test.tsx tests render states, not cache invalidation.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test that: 1) enables useDiff, fetches files, 2) disables it, 3) re-enables it, and asserts fetchInProgressRef is reset and a new fetch is triggered. Then fix: reset fetchInProgressRef when enabled transitions to false. Consider adding commitHash-based cache invalidation.

title: [CRITICAL] handleConnectionStateChange closes over stale tabs
description:
TerminalView.tsx:307-343 — Memoized with [tabs] dep. New issue tab added via setTabs but callback not recreated until next render. WebSocket onConnectionStateChange('connected') fires with old tabs, pendingSeedRef is never consumed, session context seeding silently dropped.

Test coverage: No tests exist for this callback.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: add new tab via pendingIssueContext, fire onConnectionStateChange('connected') before re-render, assert pendingSeedRef is consumed. Then fix: use tabsRef.current instead of captured tabs in the callback.

title: [CRITICAL] WebSocket connection leak on fast unmount
description:
terminalConnection.ts:78-157 — If cleanup fires between WebSocket creation and wsCleanupInner assignment, the WebSocket is never closed and onDataDisposable is never disposed. Narrow race but real during fast tab close after navigation.

Test coverage: No tests exist.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test that: 1) calls connectWebSocket, 2) resolves fetchTerminalToken, 3) fires cleanup before wsCleanupInner is assigned, 4) asserts WebSocket.close() is called. Then fix: move cancelled check to just before ws assignment, or restructure so cleanup can reference ws directly.

title: [CRITICAL] deletionPendingRef logic inverted — double-delete risk
description:
WorkspaceTree.tsx:414-446 — deletionPendingRef is set to false before the timer and true inside the callback. Rapid double-click through confirm dialog can cause two deletions of the same workspace. Also deleteTimerRef.current is never nulled inside the setTimeout callback.

Test coverage: No tests exist for delete-undo flow.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test: call handleConfirmDelete twice rapidly, assert deleteWorkspace is only called once. Write test: call onUndo after timer fires, assert 'Deletion already in progress' toast. Then fix: don't reset deletionPendingRef in handleConfirmDelete, null deleteTimerRef inside callback.

title: [CRITICAL] Concurrent drain+add after reconcileMu unlock
description:
daemon_reconciler.go:164-190 — After reconcileMu.Unlock(), concurrent reloadAndReconcile can drain the same agent simultaneously, causing double SIGTERM/SIGKILL races against the same process.

Test coverage: daemon_reconciler_test.go exists but has no concurrent reconcile test.

Approach: TEST FIRST — Write test that fires two reloadAndReconcile goroutines concurrently with the same modified agent, assert drainAgent is called at most once per agent. Then fix: add a separate drainAddMu mutex to serialize the drain/add phase.

title: GenerateHashID has hash collisions due to missing field separators
description: In internal/types/id_generator.go:30-34, GenerateHashID concatenates fields without separators: h.Write([]byte(title)); h.Write([]byte(description)); etc. This means title='ab',description='cd' produces the same hash as title='abc',description='d'. The hashFieldWriter in types.go correctly uses null byte separators, but GenerateHashID does not. Fix: add null byte separators between fields, matching the pattern in hashFieldWriter.
close_reason: Fixed by using hashFieldWriter with null byte separators. Tests added and passing.

title: GenerateHashID ignores prefix parameter
description: In internal/types/id_generator.go:28, the prefix parameter is accepted by GenerateHashID but never used — not included in the hash input and not prepended to the return value. This means two issues in different projects with different prefixes but the same title/description/created/workspaceID will produce identical hashes, defeating cross-workspace collision prevention. Fix: include prefix in the hash computation.
close_reason: Fixed: prefix is now included in hash computation and prepended to return value. Tests added for prefix differentiation and format validation.

title: MutationEvent has mixed JSON tag conventions
description: In internal/rpc/mutation.go:19-31, MutationEvent has 6 fields without JSON tags (PascalCase: Type, IssueID, Title, Assignee, Actor, Timestamp) and 4 fields with explicit snake_case tags (old_status, new_status, parent_id, step_count). This produces inconsistent JSON output. Fix: add consistent snake_case JSON tags to all fields.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit a74edb0 (merged to main). All MutationEvent fields now have consistent snake_case JSON tags.

title: RPC Client struct is not thread-safe
description: In internal/rpc/client.go, the Client struct has mutable fields (timeout, dbPath, actor) set via setter methods with no synchronization. WaitForMutations (line 366-374) temporarily modifies c.timeout and restores via defer, which races with any concurrent call. Fix: either add mutex protection around field access or document that Client is not safe for concurrent use.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit 65a47b1 (merged to main). Client struct now has sync.RWMutex protecting mutable fields, and WaitForMutations uses executeWithTimeout parameter instead of mutating c.timeout.

title: ComputeContentHash omits significant fields
description: In internal/types/types.go:130-206, ComputeContentHash omits EstimatedMinutes, DueAt, DeferUntil, CloseReason, ClosedBySession, Labels, Dependencies, Comments, and Sender. Two issues differing only by these fields produce the same content hash, which could cause incorrect deduplication during sync. Fix: include all semantically meaningful fields in the hash.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit 4374a72 (merged to main). ComputeContentHash now includes all significant fields.

title: ShouldSkipDatabase has TOCTOU race on lock file
description: In internal/types/lock_check.go:23-49, ShouldSkipDatabase reads the lock file, checks if the holding process is alive, then removes the stale lock. Between ReadFile and Remove, another process could acquire a new lock, and the function would delete the valid lock. Fix: use atomic file operations or flock-based checking instead of read-then-remove.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit ec14b25 (merged to main). TOCTOU race replaced with flock-based lock check.

title: WebUI: '1 need push' footer text is unclear — improve sync status UX

The sidebar footer shows '1 need push' in red text which is confusing:

1. **Unclear meaning**: 'need push' is git jargon — it means a worktree branch has commits not yet pushed to remote. A project lead may not understand this.
2. **No context**: Doesn't say WHICH worktree needs pushing (falcon? nova? main?)
3. **No action**: No button or link to actually push — just a passive warning

Suggested improvements:
- Show which worktree(s) need pushing: 'nova: 4 commits unpushed'
- Add a 'Push' or 'Sync' action button
- Or integrate this info into the agent cards instead of a cryptic footer line
- Use clearer language: 'nova has unpushed changes' instead of '1 need push'

title: Responsive layout breakpoints
description: Story X.11: <1024px sidebar collapses to icon-only. <768px NavRail moves to bottom tab bar, panels become full-screen overlays. Kanban columns horizontally scrollable. Touch targets 44px minimum.

title: URL state synchronization for deep linking
description: Story X.12: URL params: view, workspace, priority, type, search, groupBy, showBlocked, issue. Filters use replaceState. View changes use pushState. Invalid params silently ignored. Special char encoding.

title: localStorage migration V5 to V6
description: Story X.13: Migration function on init checking cortex-version key. Renamed keys migrated. Irrelevant keys removed. Idempotent. Unit tests for each migration path. Handle full quota and corrupted JSON.

title: Toast notification consolidation
description: Story X.14: Success auto-dismiss 3s. Error persist 10s. Max 3 visible. ARIA live regions. Position avoids FAB/terminal. onUndo callback for destructive actions. Coalesce rapid errors.

title: Focus management across panels
description: Story X.15: Panel open: focus to heading. Panel close: focus to trigger. Tab trap in modals. Transitions don't focus invisible elements. Handle trigger removed from DOM. Rapid panel transitions don't lose focus.

title: Optimistic update rollback on API failure
description: Story X.16: DnD status changes appear instantly, animate back on error. Approve/reject optimistic. SSE mutations deferred during optimistic window. Rollback restores exact position. Pending confirmation visual.

title: Debounced search with result highlighting
description: Story X.17: 300ms debounce. Matching substrings in mark tags. Works across kanban/table/graph. Empty search clears without flash. URL-encoded search param. Escape regex-special chars. Consider Web Worker >500 issues.

title: Graceful degradation when daemon unavailable
description: Story X.18: All endpoints fail: full-page Waiting for daemon with spinner. Auto-connect when available without reload. Settings accessible with cached config. Exponential backoff 5s-60s cap. Distinguish never-connected vs lost-connection.

title: Panel mutual exclusivity and transition choreography

title: NavRail icon reorganization

title: Backend availability check in selector dropdown

title: Loading skeletons and error states for all views

title: Accessibility audit for V6 components
description: Story X.5: All icon-only buttons have ARIA labels. Color-coded indicators have text alternatives. Focus management for panels. WCAG 2.1 AA contrast. Tab navigation follows visual layout.

title: First-run and empty state experience
description: Story X.6: No workspaces: guidance to configure. No issues: guidance to create with bd. No agents: link to setup guide. Context-specific empty states. Reactively disappear when data arrives.

title: Global keyboard shortcut system

title: Virtualized lists for large backlogs

description: Story X.9: Dark default. Light mode via data-theme=light overrides. ThemeToggle persists to localStorage. Respects prefers-color-scheme. All V6 components have dark and light tokens. Terminal theme syncs with app.

title: Set Seq field in hook dispatch transcript entries
description:
Hook dispatch creates TranscriptEntry with Seq=0 for all entries. The AppendTranscript doc says 'caller is responsible for setting Seq', but dispatchHookEvent never sets it. This makes sort-by-Seq meaningless and prevents ordering entries from concurrent hook processes.

FIX: Maintain a monotonic counter per session. Options:
(a) Read line count of transcript.jsonl under flock before append, use count+1 as Seq
(b) Store a .seq counter file per session (atomic increment under flock)
(c) Use timestamp-based ordering instead of Seq (already have Timestamp field)

RECOMMENDED: Option (a) — derive Seq from line count at append time inside AppendTranscript itself, removing the caller responsibility. This is the simplest change.

FILES TO MODIFY:
- internal/sessions/store.go — AppendTranscript: count existing lines under flock, set entry.Seq = count+1
- internal/cli/hooks_dispatch.go — remove any Seq-setting code (now handled by store)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Transcript entries have monotonically increasing Seq values
- Concurrent appends produce unique Seq values (flock serialization)
- LoadTranscript sorted by Seq returns entries in write order

COMPLEXITY: S
close_reason: Completed: Seq auto-assigned via line counting in AppendTranscript, tests updated and passing with race detector

title: Terminal reconnect connectFn always returns false causing spurious retries after successful reconnect
description: In TerminalInstance.tsx line 550, the connectFn passed to startAutoReconnect always returns false because doConnect is async. The backoff engine can't detect successful reconnect, so it schedules spurious extra attempts until the onConnected callback fires cancel(). This creates a race window where multiple WebSocket connections can be opened to the same session. Bounded by maxAttempts=10 and 20-session cap, but still wasteful. Fix: make connectFn async-aware by returning a promise or having doConnect set a flag the connectFn can check.
close_reason: Fixed: connectFn now returns Promise<boolean> so backoff engine waits for async connection result before scheduling next attempt. Added reconnectResolveRef to TerminalInstance for onConnected/onDisconnected promise resolution. Tests added for async connectFn behavior.

title: Git API: REST endpoints for git operations
description:
Add REST API endpoints to the loom server for git operations on worktrees. These wrap the existing CLI git helpers in internal/cli/git.go.

## Endpoints to add

POST /api/agents/{name}/git/push
  - Push worktree branch to target (calls existing push logic from push.go)
  - Body: { target?: string } (defaults to integration branch)
  - Returns: { success, message, commits_pushed, conflicts? }

POST /api/agents/{name}/git/pull  
  - Pull target branch into worktree (calls existing pull logic from pull.go)
  - Body: { source?: string } (defaults to integration branch)
  - Returns: { success, message, commits_pulled, conflicts? }

POST /api/agents/{name}/git/sync
  - Full push+pull cycle for this worktree
  - Returns: { push_result, pull_result }

POST /api/agents/{name}/git/pr
  - Create GitHub PR from worktree branch (wraps pr.go / gh CLI)
  - Body: { target?: string, title?: string, body?: string }
  - Returns: { url, number, created } or { url, already_exists: true }

POST /api/agents/{name}/git/reset
  - Hard reset worktree to branch (wraps reset.go)
  - Body: { branch?: string, force?: bool }
  - Returns: { success, message }

GET /api/agents/{name}/git/status
  - Detailed git status for worktree (richer than what /api/agents returns)
  - Returns: { branch, target_branch, ahead, behind, commits[], changes[], has_conflicts, pr_status?, stash_count }

PATCH /api/agents/{name}/git/target
  - Change the target/integration branch for this worktree
  - Body: { branch: string }

## Implementation notes
- Add handlers in new file: internal/webui/handlers_git.go
- Register routes in internal/webui/routes.go
- Git operations can be long-running — use async pattern with status polling, or SSE progress events
- Push/pull may trigger AI conflict resolution — consider returning a 'conflict' status that the UI can handle
- Validate worktree name exists before executing

title: Daemon: use lock file to detect no-work exits — don't burn restart budget
description:
## Problem

When an agent finds no work, it exits cleanly (code 0) within ~30s. The daemon's `shouldRestart()` only resets the restart counter if the agent ran for >1 minute. Quick exits increment the counter, and after max_retries=3, the supervisor dies — even though there was no actual error.

## Solution

The daemon already reads the lock file after agent exit (daemon.go:292-298) to log whether a task was claimed. When `lockInfo.TaskID != ""`, the agent did real work. When empty and exitCode==0, no task was claimed = no work available.

Capture this signal as `ap.lastNoWork bool` before recovery clears the lock. Then in `shouldRestart()`:
- `lastNoWork == true` → reset restartCount to 0, return true (always restart)
- Exit 0 + runtime > 1 min → existing behavior (reset counter)
- Otherwise → existing behavior (increment counter, check limit)

In `computeBackoff()`, use a fixed `no_work_backoff` interval (default 30s) instead of exponential backoff when `lastNoWork` is true.

## Files to Change

- **daemon_config.go**: Add `NoWorkBackoff *int` to `RestartPolicy`
- **daemon.go**: Add `lastNoWork bool` to `AgentProcess`, capture signal in superviseAgent, update `shouldRestart()` and `computeBackoff()`, add `getNoWorkBackoff()`
- **daemon_no_work_test.go** (new): Tests for the three-branch shouldRestart and no-work backoff

## Config

```yaml
daemon:
  restart_policy:
    no_work_backoff: 30  # fixed seconds between retries when no task was claimed
```

## Notes

- Lock file read is reliable: happens between waitForAgent and recoverAgent (which clears it)
- Non-zero exit + no task = genuine error, NOT treated as no-work
- This is a safety net for Fix loomcli-mkatc — handles the edge case where a task disappears between pre-flight check and agent claim

title: Implement task router with scored matching algorithm
description:
Create internal/cli/task_router.go with the matching algorithm that determines which tasks a role/agent can handle.

Core types:
- RoleConstraints: resolved from RoleConfig + AgentEntry overrides
- TaskMatch: (Issue, Score int, Reason string)

Scoring rules:
- Base: 100 (passes all filters)
- +50 per matching skill label
- +30 for matching path patterns
- +20 for priority bonus (P0=+20, P4=+4)
- 0 (reject) if priority exceeds MaxPriority
- 10 (fallback) if skills specified but none match

Functions:
- MergeRoleConstraints(RoleConfig, AgentEntry) RoleConstraints
- MatchTask(BdIssue, RoleConstraints, unclosedIDs) TaskMatch
- SelectBestTask([]BdIssue, RoleConstraints, unclosedIDs) *TaskMatch
- matchesPathPatterns(BdIssue, []string) bool (with ** glob support)

Comprehensive tests for scoring, path matching, priority caps, skill matching, fallback behavior.
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): Remove PathPatterns from the scoring algorithm entirely. Labels are semantic tags ("go", "security", "frontend"), not file paths. There is no file path data on BdIssue to match against. Use Skills for label matching only (+50 per matching skill label). Drop doublestar/v4 dependency (not needed without path glob matching). PathPatterns support deferred to a future ticket when tasks carry file path metadata (e.g., an affected_files field on BdIssue). Rename RoleConstraints.PathPatterns if still carried through — it is not used in scoring.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review

title: Add ConcurrencyTracker for per-role limits
description:
Create internal/cli/concurrency.go with ConcurrencyTracker:

- NewConcurrencyTracker(config) reads MaxConcurrency from each role
- TryAcquire(role) bool: increment count, return false if at limit
- Release(role): decrement count
- ActiveCount(role) int: current active count
- Thread-safe with mutex

Unit tests for concurrent access, limit enforcement, no-limit passthrough.
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): Remove shutdown <-chan struct{} from Acquire() signature. sync.Cond.Wait() cannot be interrupted by a channel — you cannot select on a Cond and a channel simultaneously. The closed flag via Close() IS the shutdown mechanism. The daemon calls d.concurrency.Close() in Stop(), which sets closed=true and calls cond.Broadcast() to wake all blocked Acquire callers. Acquire loop: for counts[role]>=limits[role] && !closed { cond.Wait() }; if closed return false. Close() is idempotent.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review

title: Integrate task router + concurrency into daemon supervisor

1. Add ConcurrencyTracker field to Daemon struct, initialize in NewDaemon()
2. In superviseAgent: check concurrency.TryAcquire() before spawning, Release() after agent exits
3. Extend backend resolution chain: per-agent > per-role > project > global > default
4. Apply role constraints via applyRoleConstraints(): if backend supports ToolAwareBackend, call SetAllowedTools/SetDeniedTools
5. For read-only roles: prepend read-only preamble to prompt, set denied tools
6. Use SelectBestTask in automode_poller for roles with skills/path constraints

Preserve all existing behavior when new config fields are absent.
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): (1) Remove ToolAwareBackend from daemon side — the daemon spawns subprocesses, so it ONLY sets env vars (LOOM_ALLOWED_TOOLS, LOOM_DENIED_TOOLS, LOOM_READ_ONLY). The consumer side (loom agent/task commands reading these env vars and calling SetAllowedTools on their backend) is a separate ticket. Remove ApplyToolConstraints() helper from backend.go. (2) Scope reduction: this ticket covers only daemon-side changes: ConcurrencyTracker integration, backend resolution chain (per-agent > per-role > project > global > default), env var propagation in buildCommand(), and task router integration in automode poller. Consumer-side ticket is deferred.

title: Terminal WebSocket 501 error storm: 5 backend connections retry aggressively on every page load
description:
On every page load, the frontend creates 5 terminal WebSocket connections (lead-claude-1, lead-codex-1, lead-opencode-1, lead-gemini-1, lead-cursor-1) at /api/terminal/ws. All fail with HTTP 501 and enter aggressive retry (every 2-4s), flooding the console with 20+ errors within 30 seconds.

Root cause: Terminal tabs are pre-spawned for all configured backends on page load regardless of whether the user navigates to the Terminal view. The WebSocket endpoint returns 501 when sessions don't exist.

Fix: (1) Only create terminal sessions when the user opens the Terminal view, not on every page load. (2) Only auto-create a tab for the default backend; let users add others via +. (3) If WebSocket gets 501, backoff much more aggressively or stop retrying until user clicks Reconnect.

Found during dogfood testing of drift branch. See dogfood-output/report.md ISSUE-001.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Three-pronged fix: lazy init (isViewActive gate), default backend only, aggressive backoff for initial failures.

title: Detail View with Terminal Tabs
description:
Transform the issue detail view from a slide-out panel to a full-area tabbed view with embedded AI terminal sessions. Clicking a kanban card shows full issue details with the ability to add Claude/Codex/OpenCode terminal tabs alongside. This is the largest feature epic with 25 user stories.

## Comet Backend Status
- Terminal infrastructure exists in atlas (TerminalView, TerminalTabBar, TerminalInstance, tabmeta Redis store)
- Terminal sessions/tabs API built in comet
- Git operations API built in comet
- No detail-view integration work started

## Stories Covered: 2.1-2.25 (25 total)
## Ref: docs/design/cortex-v6-user-stories.md

title: Full-area IssueDetailView component
description: New component replacing the slide-out IssueDetailPanel. Takes over main content area. Shows issue ID, title at top. Details tab is default. Back button/Escape returns to kanban. Sidebar remains visible.

title: Tab overflow handling and keyboard shortcuts
description: When more than 5 tabs, show horizontal scroll with arrow buttons. Max 8 tabs enforced. Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab to cycle tabs. Escape returns to kanban.

title: Context-aware terminal sessions with issue pre-seeding
description: Story 2.6: When terminal tab opens from issue detail, pre-seed session with issue context (ID, title, description, blockers, design). Works across all backends. Context visible as initial terminal output. Truncate for long descriptions.

title: Review workflow: Approve/Reject in detail view
description: Story 2.7: When issue status is review, show Approve and Reject buttons in detail view header. Approve changes status to open. Reject opens comment input with FEEDBACK prefix and adds needs-revision label. Both update kanban in real-time.

title: Assign and launch agent from detail view
description: Story 2.8: Start work button shows available agents with status. Selecting assigns issue and triggers loom task. Agent status updates in real-time. All agents busy shows queue info. Disabled when not in open status.

title: Deep-link URLs for issue detail view
description: Story 2.9: URL param ?issue={id} opens detail view directly. Browser back/forward with pushState. Copy link action in header. Issue not found shows error with back-to-board link.

title: Back navigation with state preservation
description: Story 2.10: Back button/breadcrumb returns to kanban. Escape when no terminal focused returns to board. Kanban scroll position and filters restored. Browser back button works identically.

title: Inline-edit issue fields in detail view
description: Story 2.11: Click-to-edit title, status dropdown, priority dropdown, tag-style label editor, dependency search/select picker. All edits optimistic with rollback on failure.

title: Comments and activity log in detail view
description: Story 2.12: Comment input with Cmd+Enter submit. Markdown rendering. Activity log interleaves comments with system events. Real-time via SSE. Author avatars distinguish humans from agents.

title: Design panel with collapsible sections and fullscreen
description: Story 2.13: Markdown rendering with collapsible H2 sections. Fullscreen toggle. Independent scrolling. Empty placeholder when no design. XSS sanitization for embedded HTML.

title: Terminal copy/paste and search in detail view
description: Story 2.15: Select-to-copy, Ctrl+Shift+V paste, Ctrl+Shift+F search with highlight and navigation. Multi-line paste warning. Copy excludes ANSI codes.

title: Tabbed interface: Details + dynamic tabs
description: Tab bar with Details as default tab, + dropdown to add more. Details tab contains current detail panel content (assignee, description, design, comments, dependencies) in two-column layout: left=metadata+description, right=design panel.

title: Terminal resize with draggable divider
description: Story 2.16: Draggable divider between details and terminal. Double-click resets to 50/50. Terminal re-fits on resize. Maximize terminal button. Split ratio persists in localStorage.

title: Show agent status badge in detail view
description: Story 2.19: When agent assigned, show status badge (Running/Idle/Errored) near assignee field. Real-time SSE updates. Click opens agent terminal tab. Show PR link if exists. Runtime duration shown.

title: Split view: side-by-side terminal comparison
description: Story 2.20: Split view toggle for two terminal tabs side-by-side. Both panes interactive. Resizable divider. Only available with 2+ tabs. Auto-disable below 900px.

title: Responsive detail view layout
description: Story 2.21: Below 1024px stack vertically. Below 768px tab bar scrolls horizontally. Touch targets 44px minimum. Split view disabled on small screens.

title: Multi-issue terminal session management
description: Story 2.22: Navigating between issues preserves terminal sessions (tmux alive server-side). Global indicator shows issues with active sessions. Explicit close all sessions option. Handle server restart gracefully.

title: Blocked-by relationship navigation in detail view
description: Story 2.23: Blocked-by section shows clickable chips with status. Click navigates to blocker's detail view. Inline indicator for resolved/in-progress/blocked. Depth limit with view full chain option.

title: Owner and assignee management dropdowns

title: Terminal session audit trail

title: Embedded TerminalInstance in detail tabs
description: Reuse existing TerminalInstance component inside each dynamic tab. Pass session name and backend. Show terminal header with backend label, worktree breadcrumb, and contextual git actions (merge/Review Changes buttons, only shown when worktree has changes).

description: Show connecting/connected/disconnected/error states per tab via colored dots. Reconnect button on disconnect. Spinner during initial connection.

title: Structured Observability: Event Logging, Metrics, Dashboard
description: Add structured JSONL event logging for all agent/daemon activities, an in-memory metrics aggregation layer with rolling 24h window, API endpoints for metrics queries, and a web UI dashboard with task timeline, agent utilization bars, error indicators, and epic progress. Events stored in .loom/events/ with day-based rotation.

title: Create internal/events package with event types and JSONL writer
description:
Create new package internal/events/ with:

1. event.go: Event envelope struct (Type, Timestamp, Agent, Role, EpicID, Data interface{}) and all EventType constants (task_claimed, task_started, task_completed, task_failed, agent_started, agent_restarted, agent_stopped, epic_assigned, epic_exhausted, pr_created, conflict_resolved, health_check). Typed data structs for each event (TaskClaimedData, TaskCompletedData with duration/files_changed/lines_added/lines_removed, AgentStartedData with PID, etc.)

2. jsonl_writer.go: JSONL writer with day-based file naming (events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl) and size-based rotation within a day (50MB default, 5 backups). Reuses patterns from internal/logrouter rotating writer. Buffered I/O (32KB), thread-safe with mutex.

3. emitter.go: Emitter interface, Bus struct that writes events to JSONL and notifies Listener callbacks synchronously. Subscribe(Listener) method. Auto-sets timestamp if zero.

Events dir: .loom/events/ (configurable via DaemonSettings.EventsDir).
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): CRITICAL FIX — Replace Data interface{} with json.RawMessage in Event struct. interface{} breaks JSON round-trip: after json.Unmarshal, Data becomes map[string]interface{} instead of typed struct. This cascades to fhr8r.3 (ReplayFromFile), fhr8r.4 (events endpoint), fhr8r.6 (OTel HandleEvent). Fix: (1) Use json.RawMessage for Data field. (2) Add NewEvent(eventType, agent, role, epicID, v interface{}) constructor that marshals v into Data. (3) Add DecodeData() method that switches on Event.Type to unmarshal into the correct typed struct (TaskCompletedData, AgentStartedData, etc.). (4) Key test: TestEvent_JSONRoundTrip — marshal, unmarshal, DecodeData(), verify typed struct matches.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Created internal/events package with Event envelope (json.RawMessage for data), typed data structs, JSONL writer with day-based naming and size-based rotation, and Bus/NopBus emitter. Added EventsDir to DaemonSettings with overlay logic.

title: Emit events from daemon supervisor and automode loop
description:
Add eventBus *events.Bus to Daemon struct. Initialize in daemon_cmd.go runDaemon(). Emit events from existing code paths:

- agent_started: daemon.go spawnAgent() after cmd.Start() succeeds
- agent_stopped: daemon.go waitForAgent() after cmd.Wait() completes
- agent_restarted: daemon.go superviseAgent() at restart decision
- task_claimed: claim.go runClaim() after UpdateLockTask()
- task_started: automode.go after InvokeAgentNonInteractive() begins
- task_completed: automode.go after agent finishes successfully (compute git diff stats for files_changed/lines_added/lines_removed)
- task_failed: automode.go after agent error
- epic_assigned: daemon.go after AssignWorktree() succeeds
- epic_exhausted: daemon_exhaust.go when hasReady is false
- pr_created: daemon_pr.go after createEpicPR() succeeds
- health_check: daemon.go checkAgentHealth() end of cycle

Pass eventBus through to automode via AutoModeOptions or context.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Wired events.Bus into daemon supervisor and automode loop, emitting structured events at all key code paths.

title: Add MetricsStore with rolling 24h aggregation
description:
Create internal/events/metrics.go and metrics_query.go:

MetricsStore subscribes to the event Bus and maintains rolling aggregates:
- taskMetrics []TaskMetric: (timestamp, agent, role, epicID, duration, success, lines)
- agentMetrics []AgentMetric: (timestamp, agent, eventType, restartCount, exitCode)
- Monotonic counters: totalTasksCompleted, totalTasksFailed, totalRestarts
- Agent utilization tracking: work/idle timestamps and cumulative durations per agent
- Prune() removes metrics older than retention window (default 24h)

Snapshot() computes MetricsSnapshot:
- tasks_completed_last_hour/24h, avg_task_duration_sec, lines_changed_last_hour
- error_rate_pct, restart_count_24h, restarts_by_agent
- agent_utilization (0.0-1.0), tasks_by_role/epic/agent
- hourly_completions (last 24h buckets with completed/failed/avg_duration)

Add ReplayFromFile(path) for cold-start recovery from current day's JSONL.
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): Replace all type assertions in handleEvent with calls to event.DecodeData() (from fhr8r.1 revision). Instead of data, ok := event.Data.(TaskCompletedData), use: raw, err := event.DecodeData(); data := raw.(TaskCompletedData). ReplayFromFile works unchanged — json.Unmarshal into Event preserves Data as json.RawMessage, and handleEvent calls DecodeData() to get typed structs. Add explicit note that this depends on fhr8r.1's DecodeData() method.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Created MetricsStore with rolling aggregation, MetricsSnapshot computation, and JSONL replay for cold-start recovery.

title: Add observability API endpoints (metrics + events)
description:
Add two new API endpoints to the web UI server:

GET /api/observability/metrics: returns MetricsSnapshot JSON (tasks/hr, avg duration, error rate, agent utilization, hourly completions, tasks by role/epic/agent)

GET /api/observability/events: returns paginated events (most recent first). Query params: page, per_page, type, agent, since. Returns events array + total + page + per_page.

Create internal/webui/handlers_observability.go following the existing handler patterns. Wire MetricsStore through ServerConfig into the handler setup. Add SSE bridge: on each event, push an 'observability' type to the existing SSEHub so the frontend can trigger refetch without polling.

Register routes in routes.go / setupRoutes().
notes: REVISION (second-pass review): CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE FIX — Move observability endpoints to the loom API server (internal/cli/serve.go), NOT the webui server. The webui server connects to the daemon via RPC — it has NO direct access to events.Bus or MetricsStore. The loom API server (port 8081) runs in the same process as the daemon. Create internal/cli/serve_observability.go with handleObservabilityMetrics(store) and handleObservabilityEvents(eventsDir). Register on the loom API server mux. Frontend accesses via /api/loom/api/observability/metrics (proxy strips /api/loom prefix). Drop SSE bridge entirely — 30s polling is sufficient for aggregated metrics. Do NOT create handlers_observability.go or observability_sse_bridge.go in internal/webui/.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Added GET /api/observability/metrics and GET /api/observability/events endpoints to the loom API server. Metrics endpoint replays JSONL files into MetricsStore. Events endpoint supports pagination and filtering by type/agent/since.

title: Add optional OpenTelemetry export for events and metrics
description:
Add optional OTLP export as a layer on top of the JSONL event system, modeled after OpenClaw's diagnostics-otel extension.

Use Go OTel SDK packages:
- go.opentelemetry.io/otel (API)
- go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric (PeriodicReader)
- go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace (TracerProvider, sampling)
- go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp
- go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp

Create internal/events/otel.go with OTelExporter that subscribes to the event Bus:

Metrics (counters):
- loom.task.completed (agent, role, epic_id)
- loom.task.failed (agent, role, error_type)
- loom.agent.restart (agent, role)

Metrics (histograms):
- loom.task.duration_ms (agent, role)
- loom.task.lines_changed (agent, role)

Spans (traces):
- loom.task (from task_started to task_completed/failed, with all attributes)
- loom.agent.lifecycle (from agent_started to agent_stopped)

Configuration in loom.yaml:
  daemon:
    otel:
      enabled: false  # opt-in
      endpoint: 'http://localhost:4318'  # OTLP collector
      protocol: 'http/protobuf'
      service_name: 'loomcli'
      sample_rate: 1.0
      flush_interval_ms: 60000
      traces: true
      metrics: true

Redact sensitive values (task descriptions, file paths) before export. Graceful shutdown: flush all pending exports in Stop().

This makes loom compatible with Grafana, Jaeger, Datadog, Honeycomb, etc. The JSONL system remains the primary local store; OTel is an optional push-based export.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Created otelexport subpackage with Exporter, Config, and full test suite (13 tests passing with -race). Integrated into daemon_cmd via OTelDaemonConfig in DaemonSettings.

title: Enhance loom daemon status with worktree details (commits to push/pull, dirty files)
description:
loom daemon status currently only shows PID and epic assignment per agent. Enhance it to show:

1. **Worktree details** (like loom monitor): branch name, commits ahead/behind (↑N ↓N), uncommitted file count
2. **Supervisor state**: consecutiveNoWork counter (N/max), restart count, last error class (NoWork/RateLimited/Timeout/Unknown)
3. **Runtime info**: how long current process has been running, last exit code, last exit runtime
4. **Backoff state**: if agent is in backoff sleep, show remaining time

Example enhanced output:
```
● drift (task)
    PID: 12345 (running 4m32s)
    Epic: loomcli-5y1sd
    Branch: epic/loomcli-5y1sd  ↑2 ↓0  ● 3 changes
    Restarts: 1  NoWork: 0/3

○ spark (task)
    Epic: loomcli-ag9nf
    Stopped: NoWork (3/3 consecutive)
    Last exit: 0 (12s runtime)
```

## Implementation Notes (from code architect)

- Extend `SupervisedAgentStatus` struct with git/supervisor fields
- Do git ops (ahead/behind, dirty count) at **read-time** in the status handler, NOT in the 5s updater loop — keeps the hot path fast
- Pairs with loomcli-ojgto (stop reason) — implement together

title: Auto-start beads daemon from loom serve if not running
description:
When 'loom serve' starts, it should check if the beads daemon (bd daemon) is already running. If not, auto-start it before initializing the RPC connection pool.

Current behavior: loom serve assumes the daemon is already running. If it's not, the web UI gets connection errors.

Implementation:
1. Create ensureDaemon() in serve.go (or daemon_ensure.go)
2. Check daemon status via 'bd daemon status' or attempting socket connection
3. If not running, start with 'bd daemon start'
4. Poll for readiness with timeout (5s)
5. Track whether we started it (weStartedIt bool) so shutdown can stop it
6. Add --no-daemon flag to skip auto-start

This is the last piece for true single-command startup: 'loom serve' should Just Work without any prerequisites beyond having bd in PATH.
close_reason: Implemented daemon auto-start in loom serve with --no-daemon flag, defer-based cleanup, and comprehensive tests

title: Redis-backed terminal tab metadata: storage, API, and SSE sync
description:
Add a server-side persistence layer for terminal tab metadata (labels, notes, sort order) using Redis. This enables multi-device sync — any browser connecting to the same loom server sees the same tab state.

STORAGE: Use Redis hashes following the fleet store pattern (internal/webui/fleet/store.go). Key scheme: terminal:meta:{session_name} with fields label, notes, sort_order, created_at, updated_at. Use the existing Redis client from internal/kv/client.go.

API ENDPOINTS (follow handlers_terminal_sessions.go patterns):
- GET /api/terminal/tabs — list all tab metadata, auto-create defaults for new tmux sessions via EnsureDefaults
- GET /api/terminal/tabs/{session} — get one tab
- PATCH /api/terminal/tabs/{session} — partial update (label, notes, sort_order)
- DELETE /api/terminal/tabs/{session} — remove metadata

REAL-TIME SYNC: Broadcast terminal_metadata events via existing SSEHub on PATCH/DELETE. Other browser tabs/devices refetch on receiving the event. Add terminal_metadata to MutationType union in api/sse.ts.

FRONTEND:
- api/terminal.ts: listTabMetadata, getTabMetadata, patchTabMetadata, deleteTabMetadata (follow api/config.ts pattern)
- hooks/useTerminalMetadata.ts: optimistic updates with rollback, SSE-triggered refetch. Returns { tabs, isLoading, updateLabel, updateNotes, reorderTabs, deleteTab, refetch }

KEY DETAILS:
- EnsureDefaults: on list endpoint, cross-reference ListActiveSessions() with stored metadata. Create default records for sessions missing metadata (label=session_name, sort_order=max+1).
- Metadata survives session death — dont delete records when tmux session disappears.
- Session name validation: use existing validSessionName regexp from terminal.go.
- Reorder: frontend sends parallel PATCHes with new sort_order values. Debounce SSE refetch 100ms to collapse multiple events.
