title: Agent Resilience: Error Classification, Smart Retry, Failover & Usage Tracking
description: Port OpenClaw-inspired agent resilience patterns to loom. Currently all backend failures are treated identically (uniform backoff, 3 retries, give up). OpenClaw classifies errors into 11 categories and responds differently: rate limits get unlimited retries with longer backoff, auth/billing errors are immediately fatal, model-not-found triggers backend failover, context overflow triggers compaction. Also adds usage/cost tracking (OpenClaw tracks tokens with cache deduplication) and session checkpoint preservation for crash recovery.

title: Implement smart retry with error-class-specific backoff
description:
Modify daemon.go shouldRestart() and computeBackoff() to use error classification:

Retry behavior per error class:
- RateLimited: 30s base backoff (exponential to 5min), do NOT count toward max_retries (unlimited retries). Use server Retry-After hint if parseable.
- AuthFailure: FATAL — log error, alert user, stop retrying immediately
- BillingError: FATAL — log error, alert user, stop retrying
- ModelNotFound: count toward retries, trigger fallback (separate task)
- Timeout: 5s base backoff, count toward retries
- Transient: standard 2s backoff, count toward retries
- Unknown: standard backoff

CRITICAL — NoWork/idle handling (from loomcli-vm8y4, loomcli-bmfqa, loomcli-2xdoq):
- NoWork: fixed no_work_backoff interval (default 30s), do NOT count toward max_retries, NEVER kill supervisor
- Current bug: shouldRestart at daemon.go:531 increments restartCount for exit 0 under 1 min, treating "no tasks" same as errors. After 3 idle cycles the supervisor dies permanently.
- Fix: when lastError.Class == NoWork, reset restartCount to 0, always return true
- Use lock file signal: lockInfo.TaskID == "" + exit 0 = no work (daemon.go:292-298 already reads it)
- Capture as ap.lastNoWork bool BEFORE recovery clears the lock

Idle polling (from loomcli-2xdoq):
- Add idle_poll_interval config (default 30s) separate from error backoff
- When NoWork, use fixed interval instead of exponential (tasks may arrive soon)
- No event-driven notification exists when plans are approved, so polling is necessary

Pre-flight gate integration (from loomcli-mkatc):
- Smart retry should coordinate with the pre-flight task availability gate (loomcli-mkatc)
- When mkatc's gate detects no claimable tasks, it enters a blocking poll loop — this is the same idle backoff

New fields in daemon_config.go RestartPolicy:
- rate_limit_backoff (default 30s)
- rate_limit_max_wait (default 300s)
- rate_limit_no_count (default true)
- timeout_backoff (default 5s)
- no_work_backoff (default 30s)
- idle_poll_interval (default 30s)

Add lastError *agenterr.AgentError, rateRetryCount, and lastNoWork bool to AgentProcess.
Call classifyLastError after waitForAgent in superviseAgent loop.
Reference: OpenClaw run.ts lines 954-1050 error decision tree

The description mentions NoWork but the DESIGN omits it entirely. shouldRestart: after the successful-run check (exit 0, >1 min), add: if exit 0 and lastError.Class==NoWork, reset restartCount to 0 and always return true (not an error, don't count toward max_retries). computeBackoff: add NoWork branch returning fixed no_work_backoff (default 30s, no exponential). Add missing RestartPolicy fields: NoWorkBackoff *int and IdlePollInterval *int. Add lastNoWork bool to AgentProcess. In superviseAgent step 4.5: when exitCode==0 and lockInfo.TaskID=="", set lastNoWork=true and create synthetic agenterr.AgentError{Class: NoWork}. title: Add session checkpoint preservation for crash recovery
description:
When agent exits non-zero mid-task, save a checkpoint so the next attempt doesn't start from scratch.

Checkpoint struct: AgentName, TaskID, EpicID, GitDiff (truncated to 4KB), ExitCode, ErrorClass, Timestamp.
File: <worktree>/.agent.checkpoint.json

Save: in daemon superviseAgent after waitForAgent with non-zero exit, capture git diff of current worktree changes.

Load: in claim.go/task.go where agent builds its prompt, check for .agent.checkpoint.json. If present, inject context:
'Previous attempt (exit code N) made these changes: <diff>. Continue from where it left off.'

Clear: after successful session start (agent claims a task), remove checkpoint file.

This prevents agents from redoing completed work after transient failures (rate limit, timeout, etc).

CRITICAL — Don't reset task status on clean exit (from loomcli-wum2j):
- recover.go:170-178 calls resetTask on exit code 0, racing with the agent's own 'bd update --status review'
- This can reset a task the agent just successfully completed
- Fix: only call resetTask for non-zero exit codes
- On clean exit (0), trust the agent updated status correctly
- Checkpoint should NOT be saved on clean exit — only on error exits

CRITICAL — Pre-flight recovery exit code (from loomcli-lb9vn):
- daemon.go:251 always passes exitCode=0 to recoverAgent for pre-flight recovery
- Should pass actual last exit code so recovery can distinguish fresh start from crash
- Skip checkpoint injection after clean exits; only inject after error exits

title: UI flicker: SSE refresh triggers full kanban re-render every 3 seconds
description: The DaemonSubscriber polls for external DB changes every 3 seconds (externalPollInterval in subscription.go:30). Any change broadcasts MutationRefresh via SSE, which triggers a full refetch of ALL issues (GET /api/issues, 300-1000ms). The entire kanban board re-renders on every cycle, causing visible flicker. When agents are active, changes happen frequently, making the flicker constant. Root causes: (1) 3s poll interval is too aggressive for full-page refresh, (2) MutationRefresh triggers a full refetch instead of incremental updates, (3) No React memoization prevents re-renders when data hasn't visually changed. Possible fixes: (a) Use granular SSE mutations (create/update/delete per issue) instead of full-refresh, (b) Add React.memo / useMemo to prevent re-rendering unchanged cards, (c) Diff the new issue list against current state and only update changed items, (d) Increase poll interval or debounce the refetch.

title: Frontend: AuthContext and ExternalAuthProvider
description:
Create src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx. ExternalAuthProvider wraps app when mode=external.

CRITICAL — Token lifecycle (two distinct tokens):
1. SESSION COOKIE — set on auth.loomcli.com by Better Auth after OAuth. Used by useSession() to check session status. Scoped to auth service domain only. Never sent to Go server.
2. BEARER JWT — obtained by calling authClient.token() (POST /api/auth/token on auth service). This is the RS256-signed JWT the Go server validates. Short-lived (15 min). Stored in authToken for fetchApi().

These are DIFFERENT tokens. Do NOT use the session cookie value as authToken. Do NOT assume useSession().session.token is the JWT — it may be the session ID.

FLOW:
- On mount: useSession() confirms session alive
- If session exists: call authClient.token() to get RS256 JWT
- setAuthToken(jwt) — stores for fetchApi()
- When useSession() detects session refresh: call authClient.token() again for fresh JWT
- All subsequent API calls use Authorization: Bearer <jwt>

Uses lazy hook extraction via getUseSession() getter (NOT module-scope getAuthClient() call — that would crash in mode=none). signIn(provider) stores returnTo URL in sessionStorage under key loom-auth-return-to before OAuth redirect. signOut() dispatches CustomEvent("auth-sign-out"), clears authToken, clears authState. Expose authServiceDown boolean.

SECURITY — Token refresh deduplication: When multiple 401 responses arrive simultaneously, the refresh MUST be deduplicated. Use a pending promise pattern. Only one authClient.token() call fires; all others await the same promise. Bridge 401 path via auth-token-expired CustomEvent listener — debounce to at most once per second.

title: Decision: Normalize JWT signing algorithm to RS256 across all tickets
description: PREREQUISITE — must be resolved before .4, .5, .7 start implementation. The current tickets are inconsistent: .4 (Auth Service JWT Plugin) specifies EdDSA/Ed25519, .7 (Go JWT Verification) says RS256, .5 (Go JWKS Cache) describes RSA key parsing with n/e fields. These are incompatible — EdDSA uses OKP key type with x/crv fields, RS256 uses RSA with n/e fields. DECISION: Use RS256 everywhere. Reasons: golang-jwt/jwt/v5 supports RS256 natively (already in go.mod), EdDSA requires additional Go dependencies (golang.org/x/crypto or lestrrat-go/jwx), Better Auth JWT plugin supports RS256, RS256 is the most widely supported JWKS algorithm. Update .4: change keyPairConfig.alg from EdDSA to RS256. Update .5: confirmed RSA-only JWKS parsing is correct. Update .7: confirmed RS256 algorithm restriction is correct.
close_reason: RS256 decision documented and verified. All downstream tasks (.4, .5, .7) already aligned: no EdDSA/OKP references remain in any design. .5 uses RSA-only jwkKey struct. .7 uses RS256 pointer identity check. .4 configures alg:RS256.

title: Auth Service: Better Auth Core Config with OAuth
description:
Write src/auth.ts with betterAuth() config. Configure GitHub OAuth (scope: user:email) and Google OAuth (accessType: offline, prompt: select_account consent).

SECURITY — Account linking (ACCOUNT TAKEOVER BOUNDARY): Enable for trusted providers BUT MUST REJECT unverified emails from GitHub. GitHub user:email scope returns emails with a "verified" boolean — unverified emails MUST NOT be used for account linking. If Better Auth trustedProviders does not check the verified field, add a server-side hook/callback that inspects the GitHub email API response and rejects sign-in attempts where the matching email is unverified. Without this check, an attacker creates a GitHub account with victim@example.com (unverified), signs in, and auto-links to the victim existing account. This is the highest-severity OAuth vulnerability in the design.

Configure session: 30-day expiry, 1-day updateAge, 60-second cookie cache (NOT 5 minutes). SECURITY: Cookie flags — explicitly HttpOnly: true, Secure: true (force in production regardless of observed protocol), SameSite: lax, domain scoped to auth service origin only. SECURITY: Registration abuse — add optional ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS env var. Set up rate limiting (20 req/60s/IP, document per-replica limitation). Configure trustedOrigins from env.

SECURITY — JWT claims: definePayload MUST include: iss (set to BETTER_AUTH_URL), aud (set to configurable value from JWT_AUDIENCE env, default "loom"), sub (user ID), email, name, role, jti (unique JWT ID for audit). NO org_id — follow-up epic loomcli-1voxb.

SECURITY — Anti-leak on token exchange: POST /api/auth/token is the cookie-to-bearer exchange endpoint. Verify Better Auth sets Cache-Control: no-store on this response (prevents browser/proxy caching the JWT). If not set by default, add it via a response hook. The equivalent of the current Sec-Fetch-Site check (auth.go:214) is CORS via trustedOrigins — only trusted frontend origins can call this endpoint cross-origin. Rate limit per session: 10 req/min per session to prevent token stockpiling.

Verify GET /api/auth/jwks returns JWKS document with RSA public keys (kty: RSA, n, e fields). Verify POST /api/auth/token exchanges session cookie for signed RS256 JWT containing all required claims.

title: Go: JWKS Cache Implementation
description: Create internal/webui/jwks.go. JWKSCache fetches and caches RSA public keys from a JWKS endpoint. RS256 ONLY — no EdDSA, no EC keys. sync.RWMutex for concurrent reads (consistent with existing codebase patterns). Background goroutine refreshes every 5min. SECURITY — On-demand refresh protection: Use a SINGLE singleflight key ("jwks-refresh") for ALL on-demand refreshes, NOT per-kid. Add 10-second cooldown between on-demand refreshes. Add NEGATIVE CACHE for unknown kid values (30-second TTL). Cap maximum keys from JWKS to 10. SECURITY — Empty kid handling: try ALL cached keys, not just first. Add 24-hour max staleness bound. Gotchas: base64.RawURLEncoding for n/e fields, reject keys <2048 bits, empty JWKS retains cache, 64KB MaxBytesReader, safeDialContext for SSRF, TLS verification uses Go defaults. Create jwks_test.go with full coverage including cooldown, negative cache, kid storm, max keys, try-all-keys, staleness.
close_reason: Implemented JWKS cache with full test coverage: 18 JWKS tests + 3 parseJWK tests. All security requirements met: singleflight dedup, 10s cooldown, negative cache, max staleness, SSRF protection, key size validation, max keys cap.

title: Go: External Auth JWT Verification Middleware

SECURITY — Algorithm enforcement: MUST use pointer identity check token.Method == jwt.SigningMethodRS256 (NOT string comparison token.Method.Alg() == "RS256"). RS256 ONLY — no EdDSA, no HS256. This prevents alg:none and algorithm confusion attacks. Add test for custom SigningMethod that returns "RS256" from Alg() but is not jwt.SigningMethodRS256. Reject tokens missing sub claim. SECURITY — Token extraction: Accept JWTs ONLY from Authorization header, NOT from query params. Query-param tokens are for opaque tokens only (SSE, terminal). In extractToken, reject query-param tokens that look like JWTs (contain two dots and >200 chars). Token size cap 8192 bytes. SECURITY — Logging: Never log raw tokens. UserIdentity.String() must redact email and name — log only UserID. Uses isPublicRoute() from auth_routes.go (.26) for route exemptions. title: Prune stale entries from index.jsonl on purge

Alternative: Filter out entries with missing dirs at query time in Store.Query (add os.Stat check). This is simpler but slower for large indexes.

RECOMMENDED: Rewrite on purge (matches the cleanup intent) + defensive filter in Query (belt and suspenders).

- internal/sessions/query.go — add optional existence check in Query

- Concurrent PurgeOlderThan + Query is safe (flock on index rewrite)

title: Daemon: pre-flight task availability gate — don't spawn agent when no claimable tasks exist
description:
## Problem

The daemon spawns Claude agents even when no claimable tasks exist in an epic. `epicHasReadyTasks()` (daemon_epic.go:162-177) calls `bd ready --parent <epicID>` which returns tasks in `review` status — but agents can't claim those. The agent starts, finds nothing, exits in ~30s, and the cycle repeats until max_retries kills the supervisor. This wastes API costs and leaves agents permanently dead.

Observed in fleet-db: ember (z0fu) and nova (x2nr) both hit max restarts and died because all remaining tasks were in review status.

## Solution

Add a pre-flight gate in `superviseAgent()` (step 2.5, between branch setup and spawn) that checks if claimable tasks exist using the SAME predicates the agent uses. The gate calls role-aware checkers:
- `plan` role → `HasAvailablePlanningTasks`
- `task_filter: any` → `HasAnyAvailableTasks`  
- default → `HasAvailableImplementationTasks`

If no tasks are claimable, enter a blocking poll loop (configurable interval, default 30s). When a task appears (e.g., human approves a review), spawn the agent. Shutdown signal interrupts the poll.

Also replace `epicHasReadyTasks` in `handleEpicTransition()` with the finer-grained check to fix the false-positive exhaustion detection.

## Files to Change

- **daemon_config.go**: Add `PollInterval *int` to `RestartPolicy`, overlay logic, default 30s
- **daemon.go**: Add `getPollInterval()` helper, insert step 2.5 in `superviseAgent`
- **daemon_preflight.go** (new): `epicHasClaimableTasks`, `resolveTaskChecker`, `waitForClaimableTask`
- **daemon_exhaust.go**: Replace `epicHasReadyTasks` with `epicHasClaimableTasks` in `handleEpicTransition`
- **daemon_preflight_test.go** (new): Full test coverage
- **daemon_exhaust_test.go**: Update `TestHandleEpicTransition_*` stubs

## Config

```yaml
daemon:
  restart_policy:
    poll_interval: 30  # seconds between claimable-task checks when idle
```

## Notes

- `epicHasReadyTasks` is retained in `AssignWorktree` as a fast coarse pre-filter
- Race condition (task claimed between gate and agent claim) is acceptable — single miss handled by existing backoff
- fleet-agent role needs `task_filter: any` in loom.yaml to check both planning and implementation tasks
close_reason: Duplicate: pre-flight gate + idle polling folded into loomcli-kv31p.2 (smart retry with no_work_backoff and idle_poll_interval)

title: Daemon-Managed Epic Branches with Per-Epic PRs
description:
The daemon orchestrates agent work by assigning worktrees to epics. Each epic gets its own branch (epic/<epic-id>) and a living GitHub PR. Agents work through all tasks in an assigned epic, then the daemon reassigns them to the next epic. Non-epic tasks fall back to a batch branch (agent name).

## Goals
- One PR per epic for clean, reviewable code review units
- Agents never block — they keep working while PRs are reviewed
- Daemon handles branch creation, switching, and PR lifecycle
- If a PR is merged mid-epic, next push creates a new PR

## Architecture
- Daemon scans epics with available tasks, assigns to worktrees
- Branch naming: epic/<epic-id> (e.g., epic/bd-spq5)
- Task filtering uses existing bd ready --parent-id support
- PR created on first push via gh pr create
- Epic exhaustion triggers reassignment to next epic

## Non-epic tasks
- Tasks without a parent epic use agent-name branch (e.g., falcon)
- Merged via loom merge as batch PR (existing behavior)
close_reason: Closed

- Assign each available worktree to an epic (1:1 mapping)

- When an agent finishes (epic exhausted or agent exits), reassign the worktree to the next unassigned epic

- internal/cli/daemon_config.go — may need new state tracking

title: Epic branch creation and switching

  2. If branch exists locally: git checkout epic/<id>
  3. If branch exists on remote but not locally: git checkout -b epic/<id> origin/epic/<id>
- Between epics, switch branches cleanly (all work should be committed+pushed by agent)
- For non-epic tasks, switch to agent-name branch (e.g., falcon)

## Key files
- internal/cli/daemon.go — pre-spawn setup
- internal/cli/git.go — branch operations

## Safety
- Verify working tree is clean before switching (git status --porcelain)
- If dirty, commit WIP or warn and skip
- Never force-checkout over uncommitted changes

title: Canonical Workspace Identity and Safe Multi-Workspace Routing
description:
v2 has the start of a workspace-aware API, but workspace selection is split across path params, mutable config names, headers, localStorage, pool keys, and default-workspace fallbacks. That creates ambiguous routing, stale client state, and cross-workspace bleed in runtime state. This epic makes workspace identity explicit, canonical, and authoritative across the Web UI, backend routing, and all persisted/runtime state.

## Why This Epic Exists

Code-verified problems in the current implementation:

1. **Workspace ID is a mutable config map key.** Renaming a workspace (`PATCH /api/workspace/rename`) updates the config key but MultiPool and subscriber maps are never re-keyed. Live bug.
2. **`initialWorkspaceID` = `filepath.Base(os.Getwd())`** which can diverge from any config name. Terminal tabs use a hardcoded `"default"` constant. Three different ID sources.
3. **Legacy `/api/issues/...` routes use `OptionalWorkspaceMiddleware`** which re-evaluates `defaultWSFn()` per-request from live config. If default workspace changes mid-flight, in-progress requests silently reroute.
4. **SSE broadcasts all workspace mutations to all clients.** No server-side filtering. Frontend is expected to discard events from other workspaces.
5. **Fleet is single-workspace-bound at construction** — `fleet.NewStoreForWorkspace()` bakes `initialWorkspaceID` into the Store. `handleFleetClaim` uses the single pool, not multiPool.
6. **Agent terminal session matching ignores workspace** — `FindLatestAgentSession` regex has no workspace component. Two workspaces with agent `falcon` collide.
7. **Log paths are globally scoped** — `~/.loom/logs/agents/{name}.log`. Same-named agents in different workspaces write to the same file.
8. **Internal worker API resolver ignores `worker.Workspace`** — always returns `wsData.Path` regardless of workspace passed.
9. **Frontend workspace is localStorage + module variable**, not URL-addressable. No cross-tab isolation, no bookmarkability.
10. **All localStorage and most Redis keys are not workspace-namespaced.**

The config map key remains the human-readable name (display label). default_workspace and workspace_order continue storing names, resolved to UUID at load time via a parallel DefaultWorkspaceID derived field. Rename changes the map key, the id: field is untouched. All runtime routing uses the UUID. Note: assume single machine for now, no shared dotfiles concern. Future: config moves to Redis.

title: Add agent stop reason to daemon state
description:
Add stop reason tracking to daemon agent state so operators can see WHY an agent stopped.

Currently when an agent stops, `loom daemon status` just shows no PID. There's no way to know if it stopped due to:
- No work available (consecutiveNoWork hit max)
- Rate limiting
- Repeated crashes
- Manual stop

- `stopReason` — enum: `no_work`, `rate_limited`, `max_retries`, `manual_stop`, `config_removed`
- `stoppedAt` — timestamp of when the agent stopped

These should be set in `shouldRestart` (when it returns false) and surfaced in the daemon state JSON.

## Implementation Notes (from code architect)

- Add fields to `SupervisedAgentStatus` struct
- Set in `shouldRestart` return-false paths and `drainAgent`
- Pairs with loomcli-fkca7 (enhanced status) — implement together for a single coherent status output

title: ResolveLockDir resolves all workspace worktrees to same lock file causing monitor to show all agents as running
description:
## Bug

When running `loom plan drift --auto` in workspace mode, `loom monitor` shows ALL agents as running (not just drift).

## Root Cause

`ResolveLockDir()` in `internal/cli/lock.go:43` resolves ALL worktree paths within a workspace to the workspace root directory. This means all worktrees share a single `.agent.lock` file at `<workspace_root>/.agent.lock`.

Flow:
1. `loom plan drift --auto` creates lock at `ResolveLockDir('/home/.../worktrees/drift')` → `/home/.../loomcli/.agent.lock`
2. Monitor calls `GetLockStatus(wt.Path)` for each worktree
3. For drift: `CheckLock('/home/.../worktrees/drift')` → reads `/home/.../loomcli/.agent.lock` → shows running ✓
4. For spark: `CheckLock('/home/.../worktrees/spark')` → reads the SAME `.agent.lock` → also shows running ✗
5. Same for blaze, falcon, pulse — all read the same lock file

## Fix Requirements

`ResolveLockDir` was designed for multi-repo workspaces where one agent runs at the workspace root. But with multiple agents each having their own worktree under the same workspace, each worktree needs its own lock file.

The fix should:
1. Store lock files per-worktree, not per-workspace-root, when worktrees are separate directories
2. Not break the multi-repo case where a single agent runs in the workspace root
3. Update all callers that use `ResolveLockDir` consistently
4. Add tests covering workspace mode with multiple worktrees

Key files:
- `internal/cli/lock.go` — `ResolveLockDir()`, `AcquireLock()`, `CheckLock()`, `ReadLockFile()`, etc.
- `internal/cli/monitor_collect.go` — `collectAgentStatus()` reads lock per worktree
- `internal/cli/automode_tmux.go` — tmux auto mode manages lock lifecycle
- `internal/cli/automode_tmux_session.go` — builds lock path for log-router
close_reason: Closed

title: loom monitor: parallelize bd calls to fix slow first render
description:
loom monitor hangs on startup because collectMonitorData() makes 6 sequential bd commands (ready, list x2, blocked, sync --status, stats), each waiting for the daemon. When the daemon is slow to start (>5s), the first render can take 30+ seconds. During this time, watch mode shows a blank screen because it uses ANSI cursor-home before printing (no output until the full frame is ready).

Fix: 
1. Run the 6 bd calls in parallel using goroutines (reduces first render from ~30s to ~5s with slow daemon)
2. Show a 'Loading...' message before the first collectMonitorData() call so the user knows it's working

Affected code: internal/cli/monitor.go lines 136-159 (runMonitor), 167-192 (collectMonitorData), 310-475 (collect* functions calling runBdCommand)
close_reason: Parallelized 6 sequential bd calls into concurrent goroutines, added Loading... message before first render

title: Blocked issues stuck: bd blocked shows 0 open deps but UI shows Blocked status with parent-child dep
description:
Three issues (loomcli-5o7, loomcli-j70, loomcli-rml7g.15) are stuck in 'blocked' status. The bd CLI reports 'Blocked by 0 open dependencies' for all three, meaning their explicit blockers have been resolved. However, the web UI still shows them as blocked with 'Blocked by 1 issue' pointing to parent epic loomcli-rml7g.

This is a backend inconsistency: bd blocked and the web UI use different logic to determine blocked status. The web UI appears to treat the parent-child relationship (--parent) as a blocking dependency, while bd blocked only considers explicit deps added via 'bd dep add'.

Fix: Reconcile blocked-status resolution between bd CLI and web UI. Either (1) both should agree on what constitutes a blocker, or (2) the web UI should distinguish between 'blocked by dependency' and 'child of open epic' with different visual treatment.

Affected issues: loomcli-5o7, loomcli-j70, loomcli-rml7g.15. Found during dogfood testing of drift branch. See dogfood-output/report.md ISSUE-004.

title: Reconcile bd ready vs monitor NeedsPlanning/ReadyToImplement filtering
description:
\`bd ready --limit 0\` returns ~150 tasks but \`loom monitor\` shows ~23 ready to implement. The mismatch is real, multi-layered, and partially intentional.

## Root Causes (from code architect)

**1. Status filter (intentional):** \`bd ready\` returns \`open + in_progress + review\`; monitor only counts \`open\` via \`IsOpen()\`. This is by design — monitor bins them separately.

**2. Blocker re-computation (bug):** Monitor re-checks blockers with \`HasUnclosedBlockers\` using only 3 relationship types (\`blocks\`, \`conditional-blocks\`, \`waits-for\`), while bd's \`blocked_issues_cache\` may track more. This creates **silent divergence**.

**3. Type exclusion (bug):** \`bd ready\` excludes \`merge-request\`, \`gate\`, \`molecule\` etc at SQL layer. Monitor only excludes \`epic\` type — other non-work types leak into the counts.

**4. Deferred issues:** Consistent between both — not an issue.

## Recommended Fix

- **Remove** the redundant \`HasUnclosedBlockers\` re-pass from \`monitor_collect.go:257-260\` — trust bd's blocker filtering
- **Extend** type exclusions in monitor to match bd's list (\`merge-request\`, \`gate\`, \`molecule\`, etc.) — add an \`IsNonWorkItem\` predicate or extend \`IsEpic\`
- **Do NOT** try to unify bd ready and monitor — they serve different purposes
- At minimum, \`bd ready --help\` should explain it shows a broader set than what agents pick up, and point to \`loom monitor -n\`

Key files: \`internal/cli/monitor_collect.go\`, \`internal/cli/taskfilter.go\`, \`third_party/beads/internal/storage/sqlite/ready.go\`

title: Create test-frontend-e2e.sh with 3-phase daemon test pipeline
description:
Create e2e/frontend/test-frontend-e2e.sh — the main daemon e2e test script that runs the full plan→review→implement pipeline for building a React kanban board app.

Follow the pattern from docs/testing/mzr-epic-branches/test-daemon-e2e.sh.

## Phases

### Phase 1: Plan (plan agents create designs)
- Source test-env.sh from setup.sh output
- Start daemon with loom-plan.yaml (cp loom-plan.yaml loom.yaml before starting)
- Poll `bd list --status=review --json | jq '[.[] | select(.issue_type != "epic")] | length'` until all 8 tasks reach review
- PLAN_TIMEOUT=480 (8 minutes, overridable via env var)
- Stop daemon after all tasks reach review
- Verify each task has a non-empty design field
- Check daemon logs for panics

### Phase 2: Review (approve all designs)
- Loop through all tasks: `bd update $TASK --status=open -q` to approve
- Verify all approved
- Verify tasks are ready for implementation (have designs, status=open)

### Phase 3: Implement (task agents build the app)
- Start daemon with loom-task.yaml (cp loom-task.yaml loom.yaml before starting)
- Poll each task's status individually until all 8 tasks are closed (same pattern as reference)
- IMPL_TIMEOUT=1200 (20 minutes, overridable via env var)
- Stop daemon after all tasks are closed
- Check daemon logs for panics

## Verification (after Phase 3)
Run verification checks and report pass/fail:

1. **Build check**: `cd $TEST_DIR && npm run build` succeeds (exit 0)
2. **File existence**: All expected files exist. The expected files are:
   - src/App.tsx, src/App.module.css
   - src/data/mockData.ts
   - src/components/Header/Header.tsx, src/components/Header/Header.module.css
   - src/components/KanbanBoard/KanbanBoard.tsx, src/components/KanbanBoard/KanbanBoard.module.css
   - src/components/KanbanColumn/KanbanColumn.tsx, src/components/KanbanColumn/KanbanColumn.module.css
   - src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx, src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.module.css
   - src/components/AgentList/AgentList.tsx, src/components/AgentList/AgentList.module.css
   - src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.tsx, src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.module.css
   - src/components/WorkQueue/WorkQueue.tsx, src/components/WorkQueue/WorkQueue.module.css
   Note: some files may be created by agents in slightly different locations. The check should report which files are missing but not fail the entire suite — the build check is the authoritative pass/fail.
3. **Export check**: grep for "export default" or "export const" in key component files
4. **No panics**: grep daemon logs for "panic" or "fatal" — should find none (already checked per-phase, this is a final aggregate check)
5. **Summary**: Print pass/fail counts and overall result

## Script structure
- Use set -euo pipefail
- Define helper functions: pass(), fail(), cleanup()
- Trap EXIT for cleanup (stop daemon if running)
- Require TEST_DIR and all 8 TASK_* env vars (validated with : "${VAR:?msg}")
- ALL_TASKS array with all 8 task IDs
- Exit 0 on all pass, exit 1 on any failure

## Reference
- Pattern: docs/testing/mzr-epic-branches/test-daemon-e2e.sh (follow this structure closely)
- Config switching: cp loom-plan.yaml loom.yaml (Phase 1), cp loom-task.yaml loom.yaml (Phase 3)
- Worktrees: falcon, nova (same as setup.sh creates)

title: Create run-all.sh and teardown.sh orchestrator scripts
description:
Create e2e/frontend/run-all.sh and e2e/frontend/teardown.sh — the orchestrator and cleanup scripts for the frontend e2e test suite.

## run-all.sh

Orchestrates the full test run end-to-end. Follow the pattern from docs/testing/daemon-e2e/run-all.sh.

### Steps:
1. Set TEST_DIR (argument or default /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e)
2. Clean up any previous run if TEST_DIR exists
3. Run setup.sh $TEST_DIR — scaffold project and seed tasks
4. Source $TEST_DIR/test-env.sh to export all env vars
5. Run test-frontend-e2e.sh — 3-phase daemon test (env vars already set)
6. Run teardown.sh $TEST_DIR — cleanup (unless --keep)
7. Report overall pass/fail with elapsed time

### Features:
- set -euo pipefail
- Trap EXIT to ensure teardown runs even on failure (respects --keep)
- Log each phase with timestamps using $SECONDS
- Accept --keep flag to skip teardown (for debugging)
- Exit 0 if all phases pass, exit 1 on any failure
- Print elapsed time at end
- SCRIPT_DIR detection for sibling script paths

## teardown.sh

Cleans up the test environment. Follow the pattern from docs/testing/daemon-e2e/teardown.sh.

### Steps:
1. Accept TEST_DIR as argument (default /tmp/loom-frontend-e2e)
2. Exit 0 if TEST_DIR doesn't exist (idempotent)
3. cd into TEST_DIR
4. Stop daemon: check .loom/daemon.pid, kill gracefully then force
5. Kill orphaned agents: check worktrees/*/agent.lock for PIDs
6. Remove worktrees: git worktree remove --force for falcon and nova
7. Remove the test directory: rm -rf $TEST_DIR
8. Print cleanup summary

### Features:
- set -euo pipefail (individual cleanup steps use || true)
- Idempotent — safe to run multiple times
- Graceful shutdown with 10s timeout before force kill

## Reference
- Pattern: docs/testing/daemon-e2e/run-all.sh
- Pattern: docs/testing/daemon-e2e/teardown.sh

title: Issue detail status dropdown doesn't update after successful status change
description:
When changing an issue's status via the dropdown in the IssueDetailView header, the backend change succeeds (sidebar Work Queue counts update correctly) but the dropdown UI does not reflect the new value. It continues to display the old status (e.g. 'Open') even though the issue is now 'In Progress' on the backend.

The root cause is likely that the IssueDetailView component caches the initial issue status in local state and doesn't re-read it after the API call succeeds. The optimistic update or SSE mutation isn't propagating back to the dropdown's selected value.

Fix: After a successful status change API call, either (1) update the local state from the API response, or (2) ensure the SSE mutation event triggers a re-render of the dropdown with the new status.

Found during round 2 dogfood testing. See dogfood-output/report.md ISSUE-007. Repro video at dogfood-output/videos/issue-007-status-change.webm.

title: D1: Daemon config types and layered loading (daemon_config.go)
description:
Create internal/cli/daemon_config.go with DaemonConfig, RoleConfig, AgentConfig, ProjectConfig types. Implement LoadProjectConfig() to read loom.yaml from cwd, LoadDaemonConfig() to merge global ~/.loom/config.yaml with local loom.yaml (local wins). Add ResolveRole() method and LoadPromptTemplate() for custom prompt files using text/template with {{.AgentName}}. Also modify config.go to add Daemon, Agents, Roles optional fields to LoomConfig.

## Previous Design (needs revision — see notes)

### Summary

This task creates the daemon configuration subsystem that enables loom to read layered config from both global (~/.loom/config.yaml) and project-local (loom.yaml) sources, defining types for daemon settings, agent roles, and project-specific configuration. This is the foundational layer that D4 (agent command), D5 (daemon supervisor), and D6 (daemon command) all depend on.

### Technical Approach

**Layered config merging pattern**: Load global config first, then overlay project-local config on top (local wins). This follows the standard precedent in tools like git (global → local) and npm (.npmrc). The existing LoadConfig() in config.go reads ~/.loom/config.yaml; we extend LoomConfig with optional Daemon/Agents/Roles fields and add a new file for daemon-specific loading that handles the merge.

**Key design decisions**:
1. **Extend LoomConfig rather than new top-level type** — The global ~/.loom/config.yaml already has a defined structure. Adding optional Daemon, Agents, Roles fields keeps one config file format. The project-local loom.yaml uses the same schema subset.
2. **text/template for prompt files** — The task description requires LoadPromptTemplate() with {{.AgentName}} support. While existing prompts use fmt.Sprintf, text/template is appropriate here because user-defined prompt files need safe, sandboxed variable substitution without format-string footguns.
3. **No new dependencies** — text/template is stdlib. yaml.v3 is already in go.mod.

### Files to Create

#### `internal/cli/daemon_config.go`
New file containing all daemon configuration types and loading logic.

#### `internal/cli/daemon_config_test.go`
Comprehensive tests following the patterns in config_test.go.

### Files to Modify

#### `internal/cli/config.go`
Add optional daemon-related fields to LoomConfig (additive-only).

### Dependencies

- **External packages**: None new. Uses gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (already in go.mod) and text/template (stdlib).
- **Internal modules**: References LoomConfig from config.go, uses LoadConfig() and GetConfigDir().

### Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. Neither config file exists: LoadDaemonConfig() returns a ProjectConfig with defaults applied.
2. loom.yaml exists but is empty: Returns defaults.
3. Invalid YAML in either file: Return wrapped error with filepath context.
4. Custom prompt file not found: LoadPromptTemplate returns descriptive error.
5. Template parse/execute error: Return error wrapping template error.
6. Role not found: ResolveRole returns (zero, false).
7. AgentConfig missing required fields: Validate Worktree and Role are non-empty.

### Example loom.yaml Format

```yaml
daemon:
  pid_file: .loom/daemon.pid
  log_dir: .loom/logs
  restart_policy:
    max_retries: 5
    backoff_initial: 2
    backoff_max: 300

roles:
  plan:
    description: "Planning agent"
  task:
    description: "Implementation agent"
  reviewer:
    prompt_file: prompts/reviewer.md
    description: "Custom code review role"
    model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514

agents:
  - worktree: falcon
    role: plan
    auto: true
  - worktree: nova
    role: task
    auto: true
  - worktree: ember
    role: reviewer
```
notes: Design revised by lead: (1) Eliminated ProjectConfig/LoomConfig duplication — LoomConfig gets one Daemon field, ProjectFile is a separate local-only type, DaemonConfig is the merged result. (2) LoadPromptTemplate now takes PromptData struct instead of bare string. Approved.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Created daemon_config.go with types (DaemonSettings, RestartPolicy, RoleConfig, AgentEntry, ProjectFile, DaemonConfig, PromptData) and functions (LoadProjectFile, LoadDaemonConfig, ResolveRole, LoadPromptTemplate). Added Daemon field to LoomConfig. Used pointer types for RestartPolicy int fields to support explicit zero values. Comprehensive tests cover all edge cases.

title: Add LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS env var to daemon spawn and AgentEntryFromEnv() round-trip
description:
## Context
The daemon communicates agent constraints to spawned subprocesses via env vars (daemon_spawn.go buildCommand()). The resolved repo list needs to be injected as LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS and read back by AgentEntryFromEnv() in the subprocess.

## Dependencies
- loomcli-y5vpk.9 (resolveAgentRepos produces the list)

## Implementation
1. In `daemon_spawn.go` buildCommand(), add `LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS` env var as comma-separated repo IDs (output of resolveAgentRepos)
2. In `task_router.go` AgentEntryFromEnv(), parse `LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS` back into `RoleConstraints.SourceRepos`
3. In `task_router.go` MatchTask(), add repo affinity scoring:
   - If agent has SourceRepos AND task has SourceRepo: +30 for match, score=5 for mismatch (below skill +50)
   - If agent has no SourceRepos constraint: no penalty (works on anything)
4. Update RoleConfigFromEnv() if needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- Env var round-trip: set in parent, read in child, produces same repo list
- MatchTask scores repo affinity correctly
- Agent without SourceRepos still matches all tasks (backward compatible)
- Empty LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS = no constraint
close_reason: Already fully implemented and tested. All 13 SourceRepo-related tests pass, full gate passes (292 test files, 7922 tests).

title: Pass resolved SourceRepos to fetchReadyIssues() bd ready calls
description:
## Context
Currently fetchReadyIssues() in automode_poller.go calls \`bd ready --json --limit 100\` with no repo filter. With server-side filtering available, agents should pass their SourceRepos to the bd call so the beads server only returns relevant issues.

## Dependencies
- loomcli-y5vpk.6 (--source-repos CLI flag)
- loomcli-y5vpk.10 (LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS env var available in subprocess)

## Implementation
1. In `automode_poller.go` fetchReadyIssues(), read LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS from env
2. If non-empty, append \`--source-repos=<comma-separated>\` to the bd ready command
3. This means the beads server does the filtering, reducing data transfer and client-side work

## Acceptance Criteria
- Agent with LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS set only receives issues for those repos
- Agent without LOOM_SOURCE_REPOS receives all issues (existing behavior)
- Verified via daemon logs showing the --source-repos flag in the bd command

title: Add per-agent stopCh and agentsMu mutex for dynamic agent lifecycle
description:
## Context
Currently the Daemon agent list is immutable after NewDaemon(). Hot-reload requires the ability to add/remove agents at runtime. This needs per-agent stop channels and a mutex protecting the agents slice.

## Implementation
1. In `internal/cli/daemon.go`:
   - Add \`agentsMu sync.RWMutex\` to Daemon struct
   - Add \`stopCh chan struct{}\` to AgentProcess struct
   - Modify superviseAgent() to select on stopCh alongside existing channels
   - Add \`drainAgent(name string)\` method: sends on stopCh, waits for process exit with timeout, then removes from agents slice

2. All existing reads of d.agents must hold agentsMu.RLock()

title: Implement configReconciler with fsnotify watcher and 500ms debounce
description:
## Context
When the user edits ~/.loom/config.yaml or loom.yaml, the daemon should pick up changes without a restart. This requires a file watcher with debouncing (to handle editors that write temp files then rename).

## Dependencies
- loomcli-y5vpk.12 (per-agent stopCh for drainAgent/addAgent)

## Implementation
1. Add \`github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify\` dependency (or equivalent)
2. Create \`configReconciler(ctx context.Context)\` goroutine in daemon.go:
   - Watch config file paths (GetConfigPath() + project loom.yaml)
   - On change event, debounce 500ms (reset timer on each event)
   - After debounce, reload config via LoadConfig()
   - Diff old vs new agent entries
   - For removed agents: call drainAgent()
   - For added agents: call addAgent()
   - For modified agents (changed repos/groups): drain + re-add
   - Log all changes at INFO level
3. Start configReconciler in Daemon.Start()
4. Add config hash comparison to avoid no-op reloads

## Acceptance Criteria
- Editing config.yaml triggers agent reconciliation within ~1s
- Rapid edits (vim write pattern) don't cause multiple reloads
- Invalid config is logged as warning but doesn't crash the daemon
- Removing all agents from config drains them all
- Adding agents to config starts them immediately

description:

1. Add sourceRepos []string field to SSEClient struct

3. Add containsRepo(repos []string, repo string) bool helper
4. In SSEHub.Run() broadcast loop, wrap client.send with filter check:
   - If client.sourceRepos is empty → pass all (backward compatible)
   - If mutation.SourceRepo is empty → pass all (backward compatible for old issues)
   - Otherwise check containsRepo(client.sourceRepos, mutation.SourceRepo)

title: WebUI: Add periodic polling fallback for SSE to catch external DB changes
description:
The kanban board does not auto-update when issues are created/modified by the bd CLI or agents. The SSE mutation pipeline only captures changes made through the WebUI's own API endpoints (WebUI API → daemon RPC → mutation recorded → WaitForMutations → SSE → browser). When bd CLI writes to SQLite directly, no mutation is recorded and the browser is never notified.

Fix: Enable the existing pollMutations() fallback in DaemonSubscriber (internal/webui/subscription.go) to periodically poll for DB state changes. This catches any external modifications that bypass the RPC mutation tracking. A reasonable interval (e.g. 2-5 seconds) balances responsiveness with load. The SSE push path should remain for instant updates from WebUI-initiated changes — polling is a supplement, not a replacement.

title: Daemon: reject duplicate epic+role assignments in loom.yaml
description:
The daemon should reject configurations where two agents have the same epic (parent) AND the same role. This caused drift to fail catastrophically:

1. drift (task, parent=loomcli-ynv4y) and blaze (plan, parent=loomcli-ynv4y) shared the same epic
2. Both checked out `epic/loomcli-ynv4y` — git worktrees enforce one-branch-per-worktree
3. When drift was killed and recovery tried to re-checkout the branch: `fatal: 'epic/loomcli-ynv4y' is already used by worktree at '.../blaze'`
4. drift failed 3x and was abandoned on `main`, where 67 junk commits later landed

## Fix

Add validation in `LoadDaemonConfig` or at daemon startup:

- For each (parent, role) pair, at most one agent may be assigned
- Two agents CAN share an epic IF they have different roles (e.g., one plan + one task) — but only if the branch naming scheme differentiates them (e.g., `epic/<id>/plan` vs `epic/<id>/task`)
- If validation fails, log the conflict and refuse to start the daemon

Currently `ensureBranch` creates `epic/<parent-id>` for all agents regardless of role. Either:
a) Validate uniqueness of (parent, role) and reject duplicates, OR
b) Use role-scoped branch names: `epic/<parent-id>/<role>` so agents on the same epic get separate branches

Option (a) is simpler and sufficient for now. Option (b) is a larger change but enables parallel plan+task on the same epic.

## Key files
- `internal/cli/daemon_config.go` — `LoadDaemonConfig` validation
- `internal/cli/daemon_spawn.go` — `ensureBranch` creates the branch name

title: Watchdog: use session transcript mtime instead of stdout for liveness check
description:
The daemon watchdog kills agents after 15 minutes of no stdout output. But many operations (npm install, go test, git push) produce no stdout while the agent is actively working. This caused 7 kills across spark/pulse/drift in a single daemon run.

## Root cause

The watchdog in `daemon_health.go:128-143` stats the loom log file (`logFilePath`) mtime. This file only gets output that Claude prints to stdout. Long-running tool calls (Bash commands) produce no stdout, so the log mtime goes stale.

## Fix

The session transcript is the right liveness signal. Claude Code writes to its session JSONL on every model response and tool call. If the transcript is being updated, the agent is alive.

### What exists already
- \`internal/sessions/store.go\` — \`AppendTranscript()\` writes to \`sessions/<id>/transcript.jsonl\`
- \`internal/cli/hooks_dispatch.go\` — maps Claude hook events to transcript entries
- \`internal/cli/hooks_types.go\` — receives \`TranscriptPath\` from Claude on every hook event
- \`internal/cli/task.go\` — calls \`SetActiveSessionEnv()\` to set \`LOOM_SESSION_ID\` + \`LOOM_BEADS_DIR\`

### What's missing
1. \`daemon_spawn.go\` does NOT call \`SetActiveSessionEnv()\` — so daemon-spawned agents don't create session transcripts
2. \`daemon_health.go\` watchdog only checks the stdout log file, not the transcript

### Implementation
1. In \`daemon_spawn.go\`: create a session via \`sessions.NewSession()\` before spawn, pass \`LOOM_SESSION_ID\` and \`LOOM_BEADS_DIR\` env vars to the subprocess
2. Store the transcript path in \`AgentProcess\` (e.g., \`ap.transcriptPath\`)
3. In \`daemon_health.go\` watchdog: stat the transcript file mtime. If transcript is fresh, agent is alive — skip the kill. Fall back to stdout log mtime only if transcript doesn't exist.
4. Keep \`output_timeout\` config but apply it to transcript staleness, not stdout staleness

### Key files
- \`internal/cli/daemon_spawn.go\` — create session, set env vars
- \`internal/cli/daemon_health.go\` — watchdog liveness check
- \`internal/cli/daemon.go\` — \`AgentProcess\` struct (add transcriptPath field)
- \`internal/sessions/store.go\` — existing transcript write path

title: Investigate and fix agents creating junk commits in worktrees
description:
Agents are creating massive numbers of junk commits on epic branches. In a single daemon run, 154 out of 160 total commits were junk — only 6 were real work.

## Symptoms

Two types of junk commits appear on every epic branch:

**Type 1 — Test fixture commits (tiny trees):**
- Messages: "initial commit", "falcon commit", "nova commit", "init", "big change", "changes"
- Tree contains ONLY test fixture files: \`init.txt\`, \`falcon.txt\`, \`nova.txt\`, \`f.txt\`
- These match exactly the fixtures in \`worktree_test.go\` and \`git_diff_test.go\`
- One "changes" commit DELETED 3,397 files (1.2M lines) from the tree

**Type 2 — Lazy full-tree commits:**
- Messages: "initial", "initial commit"  
- Tree contains the full codebase
- These are the agent re-adding everything after the tree was wiped by Type 1 commits

All commits are authored by \`test@test.com\` (see related: git config was poisoned by an agent).

## Evidence

- git reflog shows ALL junk commits were created by \`git commit\` — not rebase, cherry-pick, or test leaks
- Tests in \`worktree_test.go\`, \`git_diff_test.go\` all use \`t.TempDir()\` and should be isolated
- Pre-push hook unsets \`GIT_DIR\`/\`GIT_WORK_TREE\` before running \`make check\`
- The junk commits appear in rapid bursts (10+ commits within seconds) interleaved with real work

## Investigation needed

1. **How are test fixture commits landing on the branch?** The tests use temp dirs, yet the reflog shows \`git commit\` operations creating these. Is the Claude agent manually replicating test setup in the worktree? Is it running test commands that operate on the wrong directory?

2. **Reproduce the issue.** Run a task agent on a clean epic branch, watch for junk commits appearing. Check if \`make gate\` / \`go test\` from within a worktree creates commits on the branch.

3. **Add guardrails.** Options:
   a) Agent system prompt: explicitly forbid creating commits with test fixture file names
   b) Pre-commit hook: reject commits containing only \`init.txt\`, \`falcon.txt\`, \`nova.txt\`, \`f.txt\`
   c) Daemon recovery: validate commit tree before accepting — if tree has < 10 files, reject as junk
   d) Agent instructions: only commit via \`loom complete\`, never raw \`git commit\`

## Affected branches (from last daemon run)
- epic/loomcli-ynv4y: 16 junk / 17 total
- epic/loomcli-5y1sd: 38 junk / 40 total  
- epic/loomcli-mzgch: 33 junk / 36 total
- main (via drift): 67 junk / 67 total (all junk, zero real work)

## Key files for investigation
- \`internal/cli/worktree_test.go:347-374\` — creates falcon/nova commits in temp dir
- \`internal/cli/git_diff_test.go:42-50\` — creates init/big change commits in temp dir
- \`internal/cli/daemon_spawn.go\` — agent spawn and env setup
- \`.githooks/pre-push\` — runs \`make check\` with unset GIT_DIR

title: Add single-agent restart/stop to daemon CLI
description:
Add per-agent control commands to the daemon CLI:

- \`loom daemon restart <agent-name>\` — stop and restart a single agent (reset its counters)
- \`loom daemon stop <agent-name>\` — stop a single agent without affecting others
- \`loom daemon start <agent-name>\` — restart a previously stopped agent

This is critical for operations — when one agent is misconfigured or stuck, you shouldn't have to disrupt all other agents.

## Implementation Notes (from code architect)

**Requires new IPC infrastructure.** No RPC channel currently exists between CLI and daemon — all communication is via filesystem artifacts (PID file, state JSON).

- Add a **Unix domain socket control server** (~200-250 lines) to the daemon
- \`restartAgent\` = \`drainAgent\` + \`addAgent\` with fresh counters
- The reconciler's \`addAgent\`/\`drainAgent\` pattern can be reused directly
- Socket path: \`<lockDir>/daemon.sock\`
- Known limitation: \`loom daemon stop <agent>\` without the socket means the reconciler re-adds the agent on next config poll. The socket approach avoids this.

**Highest effort ticket** in the daemon CLI batch — save for last. Estimated ~200-250 lines of new code for the socket server + client.

title: Fix daemon status/stop detection and destructive cleanup
description:
Repro from real daemon e2e on 2026-03-22:
- daemon spawned a real planner and the planner successfully claimed a task, wrote a design, moved it to review, ran bd sync, and signaled loom complete
- while the daemon process was alive, `loom daemon status` reported "Daemon: not running"
- while the same daemon process was alive, `loom daemon stop` reported "Daemon is not running"
- after the agent exited cleanly, daemon cleanup treated untracked runtime state as disposable and removed .beads/, .loom/, and sessions/
- the next restart attempt then failed because no beads database remained

Expected outcome:
- daemon lifecycle commands reflect the real supervisor state
- daemon cleanup preserves required runtime/state directories and repo metadata
- restart or idle transitions after a clean run do not destroy the workspace
- add regression coverage for the observed e2e path
